en: The Golden Light Sūtra, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang Dynasty.
1. Chapter on the Introduction (1). The Golden Light Sūtra, Chapter One: The Introduction.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Buddha was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the great city of Rājagṛha.
At that time, the Tathāgata was dwelling within the immeasurable and profound dharmatā—the sphere of action of all Buddhas—which transcends the pure conduct of all bodhisattvas.
This *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama* is the king of all sutras!
If there are those who hear it, they will be able to contemplate its unsurpassed, subtle, and most profound meaning.
Such a sutra as this is always protected and sustained by the four World-Honored Buddhas of the four directions:
Akṣobhya in the east, Ratnaśrī in the south, Amitāyus in the west, and Svarasvati in the north.
I shall now explain the dharmas of repentance and so forth; the merit produced thereby is unsurpassed.
It can destroy all sufferings and exhaust unwholesome karma, serving as the very foundation for the knowledge of all modes.
Adorned with immeasurable merit, it eliminates all suffering and bestows immeasurable bliss.
[It wards off] the decline of lifespan, poverty and hardship, and the abandonment by the devas.
Closely involved in strife and litigation, subject to the punishments of the royal law, each harboring resentment and contention,
their wealth and possessions depleted; beset by sorrow, anxiety, and fear, struck by the calamities of malevolent stars and various evil sorceries,
with strange portents occurring in succession, they see evil dreams even while lying down.
During the day, one should remain free from sorrow and affliction; having bathed until pure, one should listen to this sutra.
With a sincere and pure mind, wearing clean and fresh garments, one should single-mindedly listen to the profound sphere of practice of all Buddhas.
The majestic power of this sutra can completely eliminate all such evils and cause them to be stilled and extinguished.
Together with their retinues and immeasurable hosts of yakṣas,
they shall all come to protect those who uphold this sutra.
The Nairañjanā River deity, the deity Kūṣmāṇḍī, the Earth Deity Dṛḍhā, the Great Brahmā,
the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the great divine Dragon King, the Kiṃnara King, the Garuḍa King, and the Asura King.
Together with their retinues, they all go to that place; they protect this person, never departing by day or night.
This is a most profound secret, a subtle and wondrous sphere of practice, [attained] over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas.
Extremely difficult to encounter.
Whether one rejoices in the heart or makes offerings, such a person shall,
throughout immeasurable kalpas, be constantly revered by the devas and the eight classes of beings.
Practicing in this way, those who generate merit will attain inconceivable and immeasurable accumulations of blessings;
they shall also be sustained and protected by the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and the Bodhisattvas of profound practice throughout the ten directions.
Wearing clean garments and using exquisite incense, they shall offer worship with a heart of loving-kindness, never departing from it;
with body and mind pure and free from all defilement, they shall rejoice with gladness,
deeply delighting in this scripture.
If one is fortunate enough to hear this, know that one has truly gained a human body and the human realm, as well as a right livelihood;
if one hears this confession and holds it in mind, this is a supreme root of goodness praised by all Buddhas.

2. Chapter on the Lifespan (1). The Golden Light Sūtra, Chapter Two: The Lifespan. At that time, in the city of Rājagṛha, there was a bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Śraddhālakṣaṇa, who had already made offerings to immeasurable billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddhas in the past and had planted various roots of goodness.
The Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa reflected thus:
"By what cause and by what condition is the lifespan of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni so brief, being only eighty years?
He then further thought to himself:
“As the Buddha has taught, there are two causes and conditions by which one’s lifespan becomes long. What are these two?
First, refraining from killing; second, giving food.”

Yet our World-Honored One, throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeya kalpas, has practiced the precept of non-killing and fulfilled the ten wholesome paths; his giving of food and drink was beyond measure, even to the point of providing the marrow, bones, flesh, and blood of his own body to fully satisfy hungry beings, let alone other food and drink.

When the Great Being thus mindfully recollects the Buddha and contemplates this meaning with a sincere heart, his chamber spontaneously becomes vast and magnificently adorned. It is composed of various precious gems, such as celestial lapis lazuli, interspersed and inlaid to form its floor, just like the pure land where a Tathāgata dwells. There is a wondrous fragrance surpassing all celestial perfumes, with clouds of incense smoke hanging down and pervading the entire room.

On each of the four sides of that hall, there spontaneously appeared four sublime, high thrones made of the four precious substances, with celestial robes serving as their upholstery; upon each of these exquisite thrones were flowers used by the Buddhas, composed of various jewels.
Upon the lotus flowers sat four Tathāgatas:

in the east was named Akṣobhya, in the south Ratnaketu, in the west Amitāyus, and in the north Svaraghoṣa. These four Tathāgatas spontaneously sat upon lion thrones, emitting great radiance that illuminated Rājagṛha as well as this trichiliocosm, extending even to the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; they rained down celestial flowers and performed divine music.
At that time, all sentient beings within the trichiliocosm, through the Buddha’s supernatural power, experienced celestial bliss; those with impaired faculties immediately attained their restoration.
To state the essentials: all the benefits existing in the world, including those never before seen, have all appeared.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa, beholding these Buddhas and such rare events, leaped for joy with great exultation; with palms joined in reverence, he directed his mind toward the World-Honored Ones with sincere mindfulness of the Buddha, reflecting thus:
"The Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses immeasurable merit, yet within his lifespan alone, doubt has arisen in my mind."
"How is it that the lifespan of the Tathāgata is only eighty years?
At that time, the four Buddhas, with their perfect and universal knowledge, addressed the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa:
"O son of good family!..."
You should not now conceive the thought that the lifespan of the Tathāgata is short. Why is this?
O son of good family!

Among the gods, worldlings, hosts of Māras, hosts of Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, humans, and non-humans, we do not see anyone capable of calculating or determining the limit of the Tathāgata’s lifespan, with the sole exception of the Tathāgata himself.

At that time, the four Tathāgatas, wishing to proclaim the lifespan attained by Śākyamuni Buddha, were joined by the devas of the desire and form realms, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; through the Buddha’s spiritual power, they all gathered in the residence of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa.
At that time, the four Buddhas, amidst the great assembly, briefly explained the lifespan attained by Śākyamuni Tathāgata through verses and parables, reciting these stanzas:
"The waters of all the oceans May have their drops counted, But none can calculate The lifespan of the World-Honored Śākyamuni."
The weight of all Mount Sumerus may be known; There is no one who can measure the lifespan of the World-Honored Śākyamuni.
The number of dust motes in the entire great earth may be known; There is no one who can calculate the lifespan of the World-Honored Śākyamuni.
The boundaries of the realm of empty space may yet be reached; But no one can calculate the lifespan of the World-Honored Śākyamuni.
For incalculable kalpas, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, and millions— Such is the Buddha’s life-span: immeasurable and boundless.
For these reasons, two conditions are taught: not harming the lives of sentient beings and giving food immeasurably.
Therefore, the lifespan of the Great Being is incalculable, immeasurable and boundless, and without limit.
"Therefore, you should now not harbor any doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha’s immeasurable lifespan.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa, having heard these four Buddhas proclaim that the Tathāgata’s lifespan is immeasurable, believed and understood it with profound resolve, leaping for joy.
When this "Chapter on the Lifespan of the Tathāgata" was being spoken, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) sentient beings resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Then the four Tathāgatas suddenly vanished. **Chapter Three:

Repentance** *The Sutra of Golden Light, Chapter Three: Repentance* At that time, the Bodhisattva Śrīsaṃbhava, during that very night, saw in a dream a golden drum. It was magnificent and vast in form, its radiance shining everywhere like the light of the sun.

Furthermore, within that light, he beheld immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, sitting upon lapis lazuli seats beneath trees made of various jewels, surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands of retinues as they preached the Dharma for them.
He saw a man who appeared to be a Brahmin striking a drum with a mallet, producing a great sound; that sound proclaimed verses of repentance.

Then, having awakened from his dream, the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa mindfully recalled the verses of repentance he had heard in the dream. When night had passed and dawn arrived, he departed from the city of Rājagṛha.
At that time, there were also immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings who, together with the Bodhisattva, went to Vulture Peak Mountain to the place where the Buddha was.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s presence, they prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit on one side. With palms joined in a spirit of reverence, they gazed upon the Honored One’s countenance without blinking for a moment, and spoke to the Tathāgata regarding the golden drum and the verses of repentance seen in their dream:
"The dream we had last night, we remember and hold fast to with all our hearts."
His wondrous form blazes forth, its radiance most magnificent; its brilliance surpasses the sun, illuminating throughout the ten directions all worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
One beholds all the Buddhas beneath trees of various jewels, seated upon lapis lazuli thrones,
surrounded by immeasurable multitudes as they preach the Dharma.
Seeing a brahmin strike this golden drum, within the sound of that drum, he spoke these verses: "This great golden drum,
with the wondrous sounds it emits, is able to completely extinguish all sufferings of the three periods of time—
the sufferings of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, and so forth."
For those in poverty and distress, and all who suffer,
this subtle and wondrous voice can remove the afflictions that oppress sentient beings;
it cuts off all fears and causes them to attain fearlessness, just like the Buddhas.
They have attained fearlessness.
The merits accomplished by the Buddhas and holy ones—having departed from birth and death, they have reached the shore of great wisdom;
likewise, the merits attained by such sentient beings, including their concentrations and factors of enlightenment, are like the great ocean.
The exquisite sounds produced by this drum cause sentient beings to attain the profound and far-reaching Brahma-voice and to realize the supreme fruit of the Buddha’s unsurpassed bodhi.
Turning the unsurpassed wheel, subtle and pure;
abiding for immeasurable lifespans throughout inconceivable eons;
expounding the True Dharma to benefit all sentient beings.
It can destroy the afflictions and eliminate all sufferings;
greed, hatred, ignorance, and the like, are all brought to complete cessation.
If there are sentient beings dwelling in hell, where great fires blaze and scorch their bodies, [this light shall reach them].
If they hear the subtle and wondrous sound of the golden drum, and the teachings issued from it, they shall immediately go to pay homage to the Buddha.
They shall also cause sentient beings to know their past lives— hundreds of births, thousands of births, and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of births.
May they cause the minds of beings to maintain right mindfulness of all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones;
may they also hear the unsurpassed and subtle words.
From within this golden drum, these wondrous sounds emerge, further causing sentient beings to encounter all Buddhas.
Far removed from all manner of evil deeds,
they have well cultivated immeasurable, pure, and white karma.
According to their thoughts and whatever they seek to achieve, such is this golden drum.
The sounds that issue forth are all able to bring about complete fulfillment.
If there are sentient beings who have fallen into the great hells, where fierce flames blaze and burn their bodies,
leaving them without protection as they wander through various calamities—
May these beings all have their various sufferings extinguished.
May the afflictions of all suffering, the retributions of the three evil realms, and those within the human world—
all such things as these— be entirely eliminated by the sound produced from this golden drum.
For all those who suffer,
who are without support or refuge, and for whom there is no protection, I shall act as their place of refuge.
Now you shall bear witness: long ago you gave rise to great compassion for me.

In every place, throughout the ten directions, the Buddhas—the World-Heroes of the present age, the Honored Ones among two-legged beings—know all the evil and unwholesome karma I have committed in the past.
Now I repent before those possessed of the Ten Powers: for failing to recognize the Buddhas and the kindness of my parents;
for failing to understand wholesome dharmas and for committing manifold evils.
Relying on one's own lineage and various treasures;
being heedless in the prime of youth and committing various evil deeds;
harboring unwholesome thoughts in the mind and performing evil actions with the mouth.
Acting according to their own whims, they do not see their own faults;
ordinary people follow foolish conduct, shrouded in the darkness of ignorance, associating with evil friends, and their minds are distracted by afflictions.
Due to the conditions of the five desires, anger arises in their hearts, and they know no contentment.
Thus they intentionally commit various evils;
associating with those who are not noble, they give rise to stinginess and envy. Due to the causes and conditions of poverty, they act wickedly through deceit and flattery.
Bound to others, they are constantly filled with fear; lacking self-mastery, they create all manner of evil deeds.
Greed, hatred, and delusion agitate the mind; driven by craving and thirst, one commits various evils.
Relying on clothing, food, and the beauty of women, the feverish afflictions of the fetters lead to the commission of manifold evils.
The three karmas accumulated through evil deeds of body, speech, and mind— such multitudes of transgressions, I now repent them all. Or,
failing to show reverence toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha— such multitudes of transgressions, I now repent them all.
Or failing to show respect toward Pratyekabuddhas and Bodhisattvas—all such transgressions, I now repent them all.
Because of my lack of wisdom, I slandered the True Dharma;
I did not know how to show reverence to my parents and elders.
All such transgressions, I now repent of them all.
Covered by folly and delusion, arrogant and heedless, I have committed various evils due to greed, anger, and ignorance;
all such transgressions, I now repent of them all.
I now make offerings to the Buddhas of the immeasurable and boundless three-thousandfold great thousandfold world systems;
I shall deliver all sentient beings throughout the ten directions from all their sufferings.
I shall establish and settle inconceivable, incalculable multitudes, causing them to abide in the ten stages;
once they have been settled and are abiding in the ten stages, I shall cause them all to be fully endowed with the perfect enlightenment of the Tathāgata.
For the sake of a single sentient being, I shall practice for billions of eons, so that immeasurable multitudes may be made to cross the sea of suffering;
for all such sentient beings as these, I shall expound the subtle and profound Dharma of repentance.
To eradicate all evils committed over a thousand kalpas— even the most grievous karmic offenses—
if one can sincerely perform a single act of repentance, all such transgressions will be entirely extinguished.
This *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama* is pure and subtle; it can swiftly eliminate all karmic obstructions.
With the ten kinds of precious jewels as its feet, it brings about the unsurpassed attainment of Buddhahood.
May the light of merit cause all sentient beings to cross the ocean of the three realms of existence.
May they fully possess all that the Buddhas have— the inconceivable and immeasurable treasury of the profound Dharma, the merit of infinite virtues, and the knowledge of all modes.
The hundreds of thousands of meditative concentrations, the faculties, powers, and factors of enlightenment,
the inconceivable dhāraṇīs, and the ten powers— O World-Honored One, may I accomplish them all.
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess great compassion; may they bear witness to my humble sincerity and graciously accept my repentance.
Because of these causes and conditions, I have given rise to great sorrow and suffering, impoverished, destitute, and lacking all means.
Afflicted by sorrow and feverish anxiety, terrified of evil karma, their minds are perpetually timid and weak;
wherever they may be, they find no moment of joy.
The World-Honored One of Great Compassion is able to eliminate all fears of sentient beings.
I pray that you will accept my sincere repentance, so that all my fears may be entirely eliminated;
I only beseech the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the present age, to use the water of great compassion—
Washing them away to make them pure:
all past evils, I now repent of them all;
as for the offenses committed in the present, I disclose them with a sincere heart.
That which has not yet been done, I shall not dare to do;
as for the karma already committed,
I shall not dare to conceal it.
The three types of physical karma, the four types of verbal karma, and the three types of mental actions— I now repent of them all.
Whatever has been done by body and speech, as well as by the mind— these ten kinds of evil karma— I repent of them all.
Cultivating the ten wholesome paths and dwelling securely in the ten stages, may I reach the Honored One of Ten Powers.
Whatever evil karma I have created that ought to bring a bitter retribution, I now repent with a sincere heart before the Buddha.
All wholesome dharmas, I dedicate them all; may the physical, verbal, and mental actions I have cultivated lead me to realize the Unsurpassed Way in future lives.
If, throughout the various realms of existence, within the perils and difficulties of the six destinies, we were foolish and ignorant,
committing manifold evils— now, before the Buddha, we repent them all.
All that exists in the world, the perilous difficulties of birth and death, the various afflictions of lustful desire,
and the hardships of ignorance— of all such difficulties as these, I now repent.
A fickle and restless mind is difficult; associating with evil friends is difficult;
the perils of the three realms of existence, as well as the poisons of the three afflictions, are difficult; encountering times free from calamity is difficult;
meeting a favorable time is difficult; cultivating merit is difficult; and even meeting a Buddha is difficult—such are these various difficulties.
I now repent of it all.
To the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who are my refuge, I now pay homage with reverence to this ocean of Buddhas;
like Mount Sumeru, I now prostrate myself before the Most Victorious One.
His complexion is unsurpassed, like pure natural gold;
his eyes are pure and clear, like deep blue lapis lazuli;
his merit and majestic power are such that his fame is far-reaching and renowned.
The Buddha-sun of great compassion extinguishes all darkness;
Pure, stainless, and free from all dust and obscurations, This unsurpassed Buddha-sun shines its great light everywhere.
When the fire of afflictions blazes, causing the mind to burn with feverish heat, Only the Buddha can eliminate it.
Like the moon, he is cool and refreshing;
with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, his body is adorned, and one never tires of beholding it.
His merit is lofty and sublime, and his net of light shines brilliantly; dwelling peacefully within the triple world, he is like the sun illuminating the world.
Like lapis lazuli, pure and free from blemish, with wondrous colors vast and diverse;
like crystal and white silver, adorned with nets of light— such are these various kinds.
Adorning the Buddha-sun,
the turbulent waves of the floodwaters disturb my mind; their taste is bitter and poisonous,
most coarse and harsh.
The Tathāgata’s Net-Luminosity can cause the parched to flow again.
His wondrous body is adorned with exceptionally sublime marks and signs;
his golden radiance shines universally upon all things, and the great ocean of his wisdom fills the three realms.
Therefore, I now bow my head in reverent salutation.
Like the waters of the great ocean, whose measure is difficult to know; like the motes of dust upon the great earth, which cannot be calculated;
like all the Sumeru mountains, which are difficult to fathom; and like the limits of space—
It likewise cannot be apprehended;
so it is with all Buddhas, whose merits are immeasurable.
Among all those who possess a mind, there is none capable of knowing them.
Even if one were to contemplate with the utmost mental effort for immeasurable eons, one could not know the limit of the Buddha’s merit.
The great earth and its mountains might still be measured;
the drops of the ocean water in a single hair might also be counted.
The merits of all Buddhas are such that no one can fully know them.
Adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, their fame is praised; may all beings attain such merits as these.
Before long in a future life, you shall accomplish the Buddha-way;
you shall preach and proclaim the wondrous Dharma to benefit sentient beings, delivering all from immeasurable sufferings;
you shall subdue all Māras and their retinues, and turn the unsurpassed [Dharma-wheel].
The pure wheel of Dharma;
abiding for immeasurable lifespans throughout inconceivable kalpas;
satisfying all sentient beings with the nectar-like flavor of the Dharma.
I shall fulfill the six pāramitās, just as the Buddhas of the past have accomplished;
I shall sever all afflictions, eliminate all suffering, and completely extinguish greed,
hatred, delusion, and the like.
Throughout a hundred lifetimes, a thousand lifetimes, and ten million billion lifetimes,
one should always with a sincere heart maintain right mindfulness of the Buddhas and the subtle, unsurpassed True Dharma they have taught.
By virtue of my wholesome karma, may I always encounter the Buddhas; may I remain far removed from all evils and cultivate all wholesome deeds.
For all sentient beings throughout every world, I shall completely extinguish their immeasurable sufferings and afflictions.
If there are sentient beings whose faculties are impaired and incomplete, may they all become complete;
for all those in the worlds of the ten directions who suffer from illness, who are emaciated and exhausted,
and who have no one to protect them— may they all be liberated from such sufferings as these.
They shall regain their strength and be restored to their original state.
For those who face execution and are beset by immeasurable fear, sorrow,
and affliction— may such persons all be set free.
Bound by shackles and fetters, subjected to all manner of painful matters that oppress their bodies in immeasurable hundreds of thousands of ways; with grief, anxiety, and alarm,
they are disturbed in mind by various terrors.
May all such boundless sufferings and afflictions cause everyone to attain complete liberation.
If there are sentient beings tormented by hunger and thirst, may they obtain various kinds of sweet and delicious food and drink.
The blind shall regain their sight;
the deaf shall regain their hearing;
the mute shall regain the power of speech.
The naked shall obtain clothing;
those who are poor shall immediately find a treasure trove, their storehouses overflowing so that they lack for nothing.
All shall receive [these benefits], dwelling in peace, security, and happiness, until not even a single person suffers.
Sentient beings look upon one another with harmonious countenances and joyful expressions; their physical forms are upright and dignified, bringing delight to all who behold them.
Their minds constantly dwell upon the virtuous deeds of others.
With food and drink in abundance and merit fully perfected,
may all beings, according to their every thought and wish, obtain all manner of music: lutes, zithers, flutes,
harps, lyres, drums, and wind instruments— such various kinds as these.
With subtle and wondrous sounds,
rivers, ponds, and pools, flowing springs and various waters, golden lotuses spread everywhere, as well as blue utpala flowers.
Whatever they think of, they immediately obtain all manner of things: clothing and food and drink,
money and precious treasures, gold, silver, lapis lazuli, pearls, jade,
and various inlaid necklaces.
May all sentient beings never hear evil sounds, nor even encounter anything loathsome to behold.
May all sentient beings possess exquisite and subtle physical forms, and may they each regard one another with mutual affection and care.
Regarding all the necessities of life existing in the world, may they be obtained according to their every thought.
May all be made complete.
May all sentient beings obtain whatever they seek, exactly as required, the moment it is thought of;
may trees of incense and flowers constantly rain down fine powdered incense and unguents for the body throughout the three periods of the day.
Sentient beings who receive [this] shall experience joy and happiness;
they will constantly obtain inconceivable offerings from the Buddhas of the ten directions,
the unsurpassed and wondrous Dharma, and the pure and stainless [teachings], as well as from all the Bodhisattvas.
The assembly of śrāvakas,
having escaped the three evil realms and the eight difficulties, encounters a place free from adversity and beholds the Buddhas,
the unsurpassed kings.
May all sentient beings always be born into noble and honorable families, possessing abundant wealth and treasures, living in peace, security, and prosperity;
may their bodies be adorned with the most exquisite forms and features, may they achieve all meritorious virtues, and may they attain great renown.
May all women become men, Possessing wisdom and practicing with diligent perseverance;
May they all practice the path of the Bodhisattvas, Diligently cultivating the six pāramitās.
Constantly seeing the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions,
dwelling securely in meditative concentration, they enjoy sovereign bliss and proclaim the True Dharma,
which all delight to hear.
Whatever evil karma has been committed, whatever perils and difficulties exist,
and whatever undesirable results are destined to arise— may they all be utterly extinguished, leaving nothing remaining.
If there are sentient beings bound within the three realms of existence,
caught in the dense and firm net of birth and death, may I, with the sword of wisdom,
sever and tear it asunder to eliminate all suffering and affliction, so that they may quickly achieve Bodhi.
And all other beings throughout immeasurable worlds in other directions—
whatever various kinds of virtuous and sublime merit they have performed— I now rejoice in them with a profound heart.
And whatever wholesome deeds have been performed by body, speech, and mind,
may they lead to the attainment of the unsurpassed path in future lives, resulting in the auspicious fruit of purity and stainlessness.
If there are those who pay homage and praise the One of Ten Powers,
whose faith is pure and free from the net of doubt, and who are able to perform such repentance as has been taught,
they shall immediately transcend the sins of sixty kalpas.
As well as virtuous women, kṣatriya kings, brahmins, and others—
if they should show reverence, join their palms toward the Buddha,
extol the Tathāgata, and praise this verse— wherever they are born, they shall always remember their past lives.
With all faculties complete, pure and dignified, they have fully accomplished every kind of merit;
wherever they may be, they are always revered by kings, ministers, and high officials.
It is not by planting various merits under only one Buddha, five Buddhas, or ten Buddhas; rather,
it is only after planting various roots of goodness under immeasurable hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands, millions, and billions of Tathāgatas that one is finally able to hear this repentance.
4. Chapter on Praise (1). *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Chapter Four: The Chapter on Praise. At that time, the Buddha addressed the Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā:
"O virtuous goddess!
In the past, there was a king named Golden Dragon Honored One (*Suvarṇanāga-guruka*), who constantly offered praise, extolling all Buddhas of the past,
future, and present: "I now revere, pay homage to, and praise All the Buddhas of the ten directions— past, future, and present."
The Buddhas are pure, subtle, and wondrously tranquil; among all forms, their form is supreme, radiant with the glow of gold.
Among all sounds, the Buddha’s voice is most excellent, like that of Great Brahmā—a deep and distant roll of thunder.
Their hair is dark blue-black, its luster curling upward like flames, surpassing the brilliance of bees, emeralds, and peacock feathers.
His physical form is beyond compare;
his teeth are brilliant white, like white jade or snow, illuminating his golden countenance with distinct clarity.
His eyes are long and wide, pure and stainless, like blue lotuses blooming in the water.
The tongue is broad and long, its color crimson and radiant; it shines with light like a flower first blooming.
Between the eyebrows is the mark of the ūrṇā-kośa, white as a conch or the moon, curling to the right and lustrous, like pure lapis lazuli.
His eyebrows are fine, long, and arched, shaped like the crescent moon; their color is a lustrous black, surpassing even that of the king of bees.
His nose is high, round, and straight, like a cast gold ingot; it is exquisite and supple, positioned at the center of his face.
The Tathāgata’s supreme marks are sequential and most excellent; having attained the true and authentic flavor, there is none equal to him.
From each and every pore, a single hair grows in a clockwise curl, soft, fine, and deep blue-black, like the neck of a peacock.
At the very moment of birth, his body emitted a great light that universally illuminated immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions.
It extinguished all sufferings within the three realms and caused all sentient beings to experience complete happiness, including those in the hells and the animal realm.
As well as hungry ghosts, humans, devas, and others— may they all be peaceful and free from affliction,
and may all immeasurable evil realms be utterly extinguished.
The color of his body is subtle and wondrous, like a mass of molten gold;
his countenance is pure and serene, like the full moon at its peak;
the radiance of the Buddha’s body is brilliant, like the sun first rising.
His gait and deportment were like those of a lion;
his long arms hung down, reaching below his knees as he stood, resembling the branches of a *sāla* tree swaying in the wind;
his halo extended one fathom, illuminating the immeasurable, like the gathering of hundreds of thousands of suns and moons.
The Buddha’s body is pure and wondrous, free from all defilement; its radiance shines universally upon all buddha-fields.
The Buddha’s light is majestic and sublime, its brilliant flames so intense that they completely eclipse the measureless suns and moons.
The Buddha is a sun, a lamp, and a torch, illuminating immeasurable realms; he causes all sentient beings to follow the light and behold the Buddha.

Through the hundreds of thousands of karmic deeds practiced and cultivated in the past, and the accumulated merit that adorns the Buddha’s body—his arms are long, slender, and rounded, like the trunk of an elephant king.
His hands and feet are pure and soft; they are revered and loved without weariness.
The Buddhas of the past and future are as numerous as motes of dust, and the Buddhas of the present are likewise so.
To all such Tathāgatas, I now pay homage.
The mind is also like this: with exquisite incense and flowers, one makes offerings and presents them;
through hundreds of thousands of merits, one praises and extols [the Buddha] with songs.
Even if one were to use a hundred tongues for a thousand kalpas to extol the Buddha’s merits, one could never exhaust them.
All the merits possessed by the Tathāgata in the present world— various, profound,
firm, subtle, and supreme— even if one were to have a thousand tongues and wished to praise a single Buddha,
one could not exhaust even a small fraction of those merits; how much less could one hope to extol them fully?
As for the merits of all Buddhas—
even if one were to fill the space up to the peak of existence with water,
one might still be able to count every drop with a single hair— there is no one who can know even a single merit of a Buddha.
I now, with reverence, praise all Buddhas; my actions of body, speech, and mind are entirely pure.
All the immeasurable wholesome deeds I have cultivated, together with all sentient beings, shall realize the Unsurpassed Way.
After this king of men had thus praised the Buddha, he further made such immeasurable vows:
"If in a future age, throughout immeasurable and boundless asaṃkhyeya kalpas,
in whatever place I may be born, may I always see the wondrous golden drum within my dreams."
I have heard the profound sound of repentance.
Now, as you are praised for your pure countenance, I pray that in future lives I may likewise attain such [purity].
The merits of all Buddhas are inconceivable; In hundreds of thousands of kalpas, it is extremely difficult to encounter them.
I pray that in future, throughout immeasurable ages, I may see them in my dreams at night, And recount them as they truly are during the day.
Practicing the six perfections to rescue and deliver sentient beings, crossing over the sea of suffering,
and only then shall my own body attain the Unsurpassed Way;
being without equal, I offer this golden drum and praise the causes and conditions of the Buddha.
By virtue of this karmic fruit, in a future age, may I encounter Śākyamuni Buddha and receive his prediction of enlightenment; furthermore, may my two sons,
Jinaratna and Jinaśrī, always be born into my family and together receive that same prediction.
Lacking protection, oppressed by manifold sufferings, and having no refuge,
I shall, in the future, act as a great protector and a place of reliance for such as these;
I shall be able to remove their manifold sufferings and cause them all to be utterly extinguished.
Bestowing upon all sentient beings All manner of goodness and peace;
Practicing the bodhisattva path Without calculating the number of kalpas, As if reaching the very limit of reality,
By means of these causes and conditions for repentance through this golden light, May my ocean of evil [be dried up].
May the ocean of karma and the great ocean of afflictions be entirely exhausted without remainder.
May my ocean of merit be fully accomplished;
may the great ocean of wisdom be pure and complete.
Immeasurable merit aids the path to Bodhi, like a great ocean replete with precious treasures.
By the power of repentance, the merit of Bodhi becomes an unimpeded radiance;
the light of wisdom is stainless, illuminating all with pure penetration.
The radiance of his body shines everywhere; his merit and majestic spiritual power possess a blazing brilliance.
Within the three realms, he is most supreme and extraordinary.
Through the power of all his merits, which never diminish, he shall deliver sentient beings, causing them to cross over the sea of suffering.
Furthermore, they shall be established in an ocean of merit;
for many kalpas in future ages, they shall practice the path of bodhi, just as the Buddhas of old who practiced the path of bodhi did.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time dwell in pure and wondrous lands;
the Supreme Honored Ones possess immeasurable merit and virtue.
May I, in future lives, attain such extraordinary merit and a pure land, just like that of the World-Honored Buddhas.
"Śraddhā, you should know that the king at that time was the Venerable Suvarṇanāga;
the two sons at that time, Suvarṇa and Suvarṇaprabha, are your two sons, Rajata and so forth, who are present now."
"In countless other sūtras, emptiness has already been explained at length;
therefore, here it shall be explained in brief.
Because one cannot fully comprehend the immeasurable meaning of emptiness, this honored sūtra [is taught]."
To speak of it in brief;
for the sake of those with dull faculties, I have given rise to great compassion and now proclaim this wondrous sutra.
As I understand it, I know the intentions of sentient beings: this body is false and deceptive, like an empty village;
the six sense bases are a hamlet where the bandits of the fetters dwell; all things abide in themselves, each unaware of the others.
The eye faculty experiences forms;
the ear discriminates sounds;
the nose smells various fragrances.
The tongue craves flavors;
the body faculty greedily experiences all tactile sensations;
and the mental faculty discriminates all phenomena.
The six sense-faculties each take their respective objects as conditions; they do not engage with the objects of other senses.
The mind is like a magical illusion, galloping through the six sense-faculties, constantly engaging in false imaginings and discriminating among all phenomena.
Just as worldly people rush toward an empty village, harmed by the six thieves yet foolishly unaware of how to avoid them;
so too do the six sense faculties each know their own respective domains, following after forms and sounds,
odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena— those very places where they lie in wait.
Like a bird cast into a net, its mind is everywhere; it constantly dwells within the sense faculties, pursuing the various sensory objects without a moment’s respite.
It cannot be nurtured; it is free from dispute and contention, and has no presiding master.
It exists through the combination of various causes and conditions; it lacks any solid reality and arises only through false conceptualization.
Earth, water, fire, and wind combine to form [the body]; they increase and decrease according to the seasons, mutually harming one another.
These four great elements are like venomous serpents; their natures are each distinct: two move upward and two move downward.
The various directions likewise have two; such are the great serpents, all extinguished without remainder.
The two serpents of earth and water are heavy by nature and sink downward;
the two serpents of wind and fire are light by nature and rise upward.
Receiving retribution according to one's karma, one falls into the various realms of existence— human or celestial— following the deeds one has committed.
When the elements of water, fire, and wind disperse, dissolve, and destroy [the body], the great and small impurities overflow and spread outside.
The body gives rise to various worms and is devoid of anything desirable;
when cast away among the tombs, it is like a decayed log.
Virtuous daughter, you should observe that all phenomena are thus: where is there any person?
As for sentient beings and these great elements: each and every one is unreal; fundamentally they are unarisen, and by nature they lack conjunction.
For these reasons, I say that the great elements are fundamentally unreal from the beginning, existing only through combination;
the essence and characteristics of ignorance likewise do not exist inherently from the beginning, but exist through the combination of causes and conditions of deluded conceptualization.
Because they have no substantial reality, they are conventionally designated as "ignorance. Therefore, I say:
Known as ignorance, volitional formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases,
contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, old age, death, sorrow, and affliction—
these manifold activities of suffering are inconceivable; birth and death are without end, revolving without ceasing.
Fundamentally there is no arising, nor is there any combination; it is produced by the mental activities of unwholesome reflection.
I have severed all fetters of views and the like, and with the sword of wisdom, I have rent asunder the web of afflictions.
Contemplating the five aggregates as a house, one realizes they are entirely empty and quiescent; thus one attains the unsurpassed path and its subtle, wondrous merit.

Opening the gate of ambrosia, displaying the vessel of ambrosia, entering the city of ambrosia, and dwelling in the chamber of ambrosia, one causes all sentient beings to partake of the flavor of ambrosia.
Blowing the great Dharma conch, beating the great Dharma drum, kindling the great Dharma torch,
and raining down the supreme Dharma rain;
I now subdue all enmities and fetters, and raise aloft the foremost, subtle, and wondrous Dharma banner.
To deliver all sentient beings from the ocean of birth and death, forever severing the three evil realms and immeasurable suffering and affliction;
for afflictions blaze fiercely, burning all sentient beings who have no rescue or protection and no place of refuge.
Providing for these beings, causing them to be free from the fever of affliction, they have, throughout immeasurable eons,
practiced various deeds in accordance with the path, making offerings and showing reverence to the Buddhas,
the World-Honored Ones; steadfastly cultivating the Way to Bodhi.
They sought from the Tathāgata the true Dharma-body;
heads, eyes, marrow, and brains; beloved wives and children; money, wealth, and treasures;
pearls and necklaces; gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and various other extraordinary things.
The Golden Light Sūtra, Volume One;
The Golden Light Sūtra, Volume Two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Six: The Four Heavenly Kings (*Caturmahārājakāyika*) The Sixth Chapter of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*: The Four Heavenly Kings.

At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, and the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa all rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, knelt with their right knees on the ground, joined their palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! [...]”

This subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra is the king of all sūtras; it is protected and remembered by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; it adorns the profound and wondrous merits of Bodhisattvas; it is constantly revered by the various devas; it causes the hearts of the celestial kings to rejoice; and it is also praised by the World-Protectors.

This sutra can illuminate the palaces of all the devas; this sutra can bestow happiness upon sentient beings; this sutra can cause the rivers of the hells, hungry ghosts, and animals to wither and dry up; this sutra can eliminate all fears; this sutra can repel enemies and bandits from other regions; this sutra can remove the calamity of famine and high grain prices; this sutra can cure all pestilential diseases; this sutra can extinguish the portents of malevolent stars; and this sutra can eliminate all sorrow and affliction.
To state the essentials: this sutra can extinguish the immeasurable, boundless, hundreds of thousands of sufferings and afflictions of all sentient beings.
"World-Honored One!

When this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra is extensively proclaimed among the great assembly, we, the Four Kings and our other retinues, having heard this supreme nectar-like flavor of the Dharma, shall increase our physical strength, mental vigor, and courage, and be endowed with all majestic virtues."
“World-Honored One!
We four kings can preach the true Dharma and practice the true Dharma, acting as Dharma-kings of the world to govern the world according to the Dharma.
World-Honored One!”

We four kings, along with the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, shall govern the world according to the Dharma and ward off all evil spirits who consume vital essence.
“World-Honored One!

We, the four kings and the various spirits and ghosts of the twenty-eight divisions, along with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of spirits and ghosts, with our pure divine eyes that surpass those of humans, constantly observe and protect this Jambudvīpa.”
World-Honored One!
For this reason, we are called the World-Protecting Kings.

If in this land there should be various depletions, enemies invading the borders, famine, pestilence, or various kinds of hardships, and if there should be a bhikṣu who upholds this sutra, we, the four kings, shall together exhort him so that, by our power, he may swiftly go to those kingdoms, cities, districts, and counties to widely proclaim and disseminate this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra, causing all such various hundreds of thousands of depleting matters to be entirely extinguished.
“World-Honored One!

Just as there are territories belonging to various kings, if a holder of this sutra should arrive in their kingdom, that king ought to go to that person’s place to hear and receive such a subtle and wondrous sutra. Having heard it, he shall rejoice; furthermore, he shall protect, mindfully attend to, and revere that person.”
“World-Honored One!

We, the four kings, shall further diligently protect this king, as well as the people of his realm, with a devoted mind, to eliminate their misfortunes and afflictions so that they may attain peace and security.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who receive and uphold this sutra, and if there are kings among men who are able to provide for them and bestow upon them all that they need for their well-being, we, the four kings, shall likewise cause these kings, as well as all the people of their kingdoms, to be entirely secure, peaceful, and free from all affliction.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are members of the fourfold assembly who receive, uphold, read, and recite this sublime sūtra, and if there are kings among men who are able to make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise them;

we, the Four Kings, shall likewise cause such kings among men to always receive the foremost offerings, reverence, respect, and praise among all kings, and shall also cause other kings to look up to them with admiration, envy, and to praise their goodness.”
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Four Heavenly Kings who protect the world, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!

You Four Kings, in the past you have already made offerings to, paid homage to, revered, and praised immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas. Having planted various roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas, you have preached the True Dharma and practiced the True Dharma, governing the world according to the Dharma as kings of men and gods."

Today you have brought long-term benefit to all sentient beings; practicing great compassion, you bestow upon them every requisite for happiness, able to restrain all evils and diligently encourage all virtues.

For this reason, if there is a king who is able to make offerings to and revere this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, you should truly protect and mind him in such a manner, extinguishing his suffering and distress and bestowing upon him peace and happiness.

“If you, the four kings and your retinues, along with immeasurable and boundless hundreds of thousands of spirits and deities, are able to protect and keep in mind a sūtra such as this, you will thereby be upholding the true Dharma of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”
When you, the four kings, along with the other hosts of devas and hundreds of thousands of spirits and deities, engage in battle with the asuras, you gods shall always achieve victory.
If you are able to protect and keep this sutra in mind, you will be able to eliminate and subdue all sufferings, namely those caused by enemies, thieves, famine, and pestilence.

If any members of the fourfold assembly can receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, you should also diligently protect them with a devoted heart, removing their decline and afflictions and bestowing upon them peace and happiness.
At that time, the Four Kings again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra shall circulate in future ages wherever it may reach—whether in kingdoms, cities, prefectures, counties, villages, or hamlets. If the kings of those lands govern the world according to celestial laws, and can further reverently and with sincere heart listen to and receive this sublime sūtra, and moreover honor, make offerings to, and provide for the fourfold assembly who uphold this sūtra, then by these causes and conditions, we shall from time to time hear such a subtle and wondrous sūtra. Having heard it, we shall immediately gain an increase in physical strength, our minds will become courageous and resolute, and we shall be endowed with all majestic virtues.”
Therefore, we and immeasurable spirits shall constantly remain invisible and follow wherever this sublime scripture is disseminated, providing protection so that no obstacles arise;

we shall also guard and mind the kings and their subjects who listen to this sutra, removing their hardships and afflictions so that all may dwell in peace and security, and causing enemies and bandits from other regions to retreat and disperse.
World-Honored One! If there is a king who listens to this sutra, and the hostile enemies of neighboring states conceive such a thought as:
"We shall assemble the fourfold army to destroy that kingdom.
World-Honored One!

By the majestic spiritual power of this sutra, at that time, neighboring enemies and other adversaries will create obstacles and difficulties, giving rise to various forms of decline, affliction, calamities, and pestilence within their territories.
At that time, when the enemies have committed such evil deeds as these, they shall assemble their fourfold army and set out toward this country, intending to wage war and inflict punishment.

At that time, we, together with our retinues of immeasurable and boundless hundreds of thousands of spirits and deities, shall conceal our forms and provide protection and assistance, causing those enemies to naturally retreat and disperse, and instilling in them various terrors and obstacles.
“If even the military forces of that country cannot reach there, how much less could they possibly cause any destruction?
At that time, the Buddha praised the Four Heavenly Kings and the others:
“Excellent, excellent!”

"You Four Kings, you are indeed able to protect my cultivation of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayuta* kalpas, as well as those kings among men who uphold this sutra, reverently making offerings to it; you shall eliminate their misfortunes and afflictions to bring them peace and happiness.

Furthermore, you are able to protect their palaces, residences, cities, towns, villages, kingdoms, and frontiers, even driving back all enemies and bandits so that they disperse, extinguishing their decline and distress to grant them security. You shall also ensure that all kings within Jambudvīpa are free from calamities, strife, and litigation."

"O Four Kings, you should know that in this Jambudvīpa there are eighty-four thousand cities, towns, and villages, and eighty-four thousand human kings. Each enjoys pleasure and happiness within his own kingdom, and each attains sovereignty over his own realm.
Regarding their respective wealth and treasures, each is self-sufficient and does not encroach upon or seize from another;

according to the karma they have cultivated and accumulated in past lives, they receive retribution in accordance with that karma, and they do not give rise to evil thoughts or covet the lands of others."

Each will give rise to a mind of self-benefit, a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of peace and happiness, a mind free from contention, a mind free from destruction, a mind free from bondage, and a mind free from violence; each will naturally develop affection for their own land, with those above and below living in harmony like water and milk, their hearts cherishing one another and increasing all roots of goodness.

For these reasons, this Jambudvīpa is peaceful, secure, and prosperous; its population is flourishing and the earth is fertile. Yin and yang are harmonized, the seasons do not deviate from their order, and the sun, moon, and stars do not lose their regular courses. Wind and rain arrive at their proper times, and there are no calamities or misfortunes. The people are abundant and self-sufficient in wealth; their hearts are free from greed and stinginess, as well as envy. They practice the ten wholesome deeds equally, and when their lives end, most are reborn in the heavens, filling the celestial palaces and increasing the ranks of the devas.

“If, in future ages, there are kings who listen to this sutra and who offer worship, respect, and uphold this sutra along with the fourfold assembly, those kings will bring peace, happiness, benefit, and welfare to you, the Four Kings, as well as to your retinues and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of spirits.”
For what reason?

O Four Kings, if you should hear this sutra from time to time, you will have already obtained the water of the True Dharma; by partaking of the flavor of ambrosia, your physical strength will increase, your mind will become courageous and sharp, and you will be endowed with all majestic virtues.
If these kings of men can listen to and receive this sutra with a sincere heart, they will have already been able to make offerings to me.
If they make offerings to me, they are making offerings to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
and if they can make offerings to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, they will obtain an immeasurable and inconceivable mass of merit.

By these causes and conditions, these kings of men should receive protection; likewise, their queens, concubines, ladies of the inner palace, retinues, and princes should also receive protection. Their decline and afflictions shall be extinguished, and their happiness shall flourish. Their palaces, halls, and buildings shall be peaceful, secure, and pure, free from all calamities and portents. The deities who protect the dwellings shall increase in majesty and virtue, and they too shall experience immeasurable joy and bliss.
"In all these lands, the inhabitants shall fully enjoy the various pleasures of the five senses, and all evil matters shall be completely extinguished.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

In future ages, if there should be a king who desires to protect himself, his queens, concubines, and princes, as well as his palaces and residences; who desires to obtain the foremost protection for his person such that his reign becomes most preeminent and he possesses the inconceivable merits of a sovereign;
and who desires to gather an immeasurable mass of merit so that his realm is free from the enmity of foreign invaders and devoid of all anxieties, afflictions, and painful matters.
“World-Honored One!

Such a king of men should not be negligent or allow his mind to be distracted; he should give rise to a heart of reverence and humility. He should adorn his foremost, most subtle, and most excellent palace with various fragrant liquids used to sprinkle the ground, scatter various flowers, and spread a great Dharma-seat—a lion-throne—further embellished with immeasurable rare and extraordinary treasures, and hung with various countless, subtle, and exquisite banners, streamers, and jeweled canopies.”

One should bathe and purify oneself, anointing the body with fragrances and adorning oneself with fine, clean garments and necklaces. Sitting upon a low seat rather than exalting oneself, one should cast off self-importance and remain free from all negligence. Being humble and self-effacing, one should eliminate pride and listen to such sublime scriptures with right mindfulness, regarding the Dharma-preacher as the World-Honored One.

Furthermore, toward the queens, princes, court ladies, and retinues within the palace, one should give rise to a heart of compassion and address them with a serene countenance, encouraging them to provide various offerings to the Dharma-master.

At that time, having thus exhorted and transformed others, the king immediately gave rise to immeasurable joy and happiness; with a heart full of delight, he redoubled his self-exertion, never succumbing to weariness as he performed many acts of benefit, and he conceived even greater reverence for the Dharma-preacher.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Four Great Heavenly Kings:

"The king of men at that time should don pure, clean, and fresh garments, adorned with various necklaces arranged in perfect order; holding a subtle, supreme white parasol, his attire and deportment remaining constant and proper, he should personally go out to welcome the one who preaches the Dharma."
Why is this? Because with every single step this king takes, he is making offerings to and meeting hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones;
furthermore, he attains transcendence from the perils of birth and death for as many eons as there are steps.
Furthermore, throughout as many eons as there are in the future world, they shall constantly receive the consecration and attain the rank of a universal monarch (cakravartin);
with every step they take, they shall likewise obtain such inconceivable and sovereign power of merit in the present life;
and they shall always obtain the most supreme and exquisite palaces of the seven treasures for humans and devas.
In every place of rebirth, one’s lifespan shall increase;
one’s speech shall be eloquent and clear, such that people place their trust in it;
free from fear or apprehension, one shall attain great renown.
They are constantly revered by humans and devas, experiencing supreme and wondrous bliss among gods and men;
they attain great power and are endowed with majestic virtue;
their physical form is subtle and exquisite, being foremost in its dignified beauty.
They shall constantly encounter the Buddhas and meet with spiritual friends;
they shall achieve and be fully endowed with immeasurable accumulations of merit.
"O you Four Heavenly Kings!
When a king of men perceives such various and immeasurable merits and benefits as these, he ought to personally go forth to welcome the Dharma Master;
whether the distance be one *yojana* or even a hundred thousand *yojanas*, he should conceive of the Dharma Master as a Buddha and think thus:

"Today, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, with his true wisdom, enters my palace to receive my offerings and preach the Dharma for me. By hearing this Dharma, I shall not regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; I have already encountered hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nayutas* of Buddhas; I have already made offerings to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present; and I have attained the ultimate cessation of the sufferings of the three evil realms."

I have now planted the causes for becoming a hundred thousand immeasurable wheel-turning kings, Śakras, and Brahmās; I have planted the seeds of boundless roots of goodness; I have enabled immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings to cross over birth and death; I have accumulated immeasurable and boundless masses of merit; my harem and retinue have already obtained protection; all misfortunes within my palace and residence have been entirely extinguished; my realm is free from enemies, bandits, and thorns; and hostile adversaries from other regions cannot invade or oppress it.

“O you Four Kings! Such a king of men should perform such offerings to the True Dharma, purely listening to and receiving this sublime sutra, as well as reverently making offerings to, honoring, and praising the fourfold assembly who uphold this sutra;
he should also dedicate a portion of the most supreme merit thus obtained to you and your other retinues of devas, ghosts, and spirits.”

By gathering such virtuous merits, one will constantly obtain immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable benefits of mastery in the present life; with majestic power and influence fully perfected, one will be able to subdue all evils through the True Dharma.
At that time, the Four Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If in future ages there are various kings who thus revere the True Dharma, wholeheartedly listen to and receive this sublime sūtra, and who likewise revere, make offerings to, respect, and praise the fourfold assembly that upholds this sūtra; and when they have adorned their dwellings, sprinkled the ground with fragrant liquid, and listen to the preaching of the Dharma with single-minded right mindfulness, we Four Kings shall also be present among them to hear this Dharma together. We pray that these human kings, for the sake of their own benefit, will bestow a small portion of the merit they have obtained upon us.”
“World-Honored One!

When these kings of men, for our sake, burn various kinds of incense as an offering to this sutra at the place where the Dharma-preachers sit, that wondrous fragrance reaches our celestial palaces in a single thought-moment. That fragrance immediately transforms into fragrant canopies; its subtle and exquisite golden radiance shines upon our palaces, the palaces of Śakra, and the palaces of Brahmā.”

The Great Eloquence Deity, the Virtue Deity, the Earth Goddess Sthāvarā, the Spirit Vaiśravaṇa, the Great General, the Great Generals of the twenty-eight divisions of spirits, Maheśvara, Vajrapāṇi, the Spirit General Maṇibhadra, and Hārītī surrounded by her five hundred sons; as well as the Naga King Anavatapta, the Naga King Sāgara, and suchlike multitudes—each within their own palaces perceived this wondrous fragrance and beheld the light of the incense-canopy shining everywhere, that light of the incense-canopy also illuminating the palaces of all the devas.
The Buddha told the Four Kings:
"This radiance from the fragrant canopy does not merely reach your palaces, O Four Kings. Why is this?"

When these kings of men hold incense burners in their hands to make offerings during the recitation of the sutra, the fragrance spreads everywhere; in a single thought-moment, it reaches throughout the trichiliocosm, including ten billion suns and moons, ten billion great oceans, ten billion Sumeru mountains, ten billion Great Iron Ring Mountains and Small Iron Ring Mountains as well as all the kings of mountains;
ten billion sets of four continents, ten billion Four Heavenly Kings, ten billion Trāyastriṃśa heavens, and so on, up to ten billion Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana heavens.

Within this great trichiliocosm, throughout the ten billion heavens of the Thirty-three Gods, and among all the palaces of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas in the void of space, various clouds of incense smoke completely filled the air; the golden light from those canopies also illuminated the palaces.
Thus, all the various clouds of incense smoke and canopies that exist throughout this trichiliocosm are due to the majestic spiritual power of this sutra.

When these kings of men hold incense burners in their hands to make offerings to the sutra, the various fragrances not only pervade this trichiliocosm, but in a single thought-moment, they also pervade hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of immeasurable and boundless Ganges Rivers throughout the ten directions. Furthermore, within the void above those Buddhas, they likewise form canopies of fragrance, and the universal radiance of golden light is just the same.

When the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, heard this wondrous fragrance, saw these fragrant canopies and golden light, and had performed such supernatural transformations throughout Buddha-worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, they praised the speaker of the Dharma with one voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"O Mahāsattva!

You are able to widely proclaim and disseminate such a profound and subtle sūtra; you shall thereby accomplish a mass of immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable merit. If anyone hears this profound sūtra, the merit they obtain will not be small, let alone those who uphold, read, recite it, and for the sake of other sentient beings, reveal, analyze, and expound its meaning."

Why is this? Good son! If immeasurable, boundless billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas should hear this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra, they will immediately never retreat from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the Buddhas currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions—worlds as numerous as the sands of immeasurable and boundless Ganges Rivers—spoke with one voice in unison, saying:
"O son of good family!..."

In a future age, you will certainly attain the seat of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree; most honored and most supreme within the triple world, you shall transcend all sentient beings. Through the power of diligent cultivation, you will undergo various ascetic practices, skillfully adorning the site of enlightenment. You will be able to destroy the heterodox arguments of the outsiders throughout the trichiliocosm and subdue the various demonic enemies and adversaries in their diverse forms. You shall awaken to the path of supreme, quiescent, pure, stainless, and profound, unsurpassed bodhi, which is the realization of all dharmas.

“Good son! You have already been able to sit upon the Vajra Seat and turn the twelvefold wheel of Dharma—profound and praised by all Buddhas—which is unsurpassed; you have been able to beat the unsurpassed, greatest drum of Dharma; you have been able to blow the unsurpassed, most exquisite conch of Dharma; you have been able to raise the unsurpassed, most supreme banner of Dharma; you have been able to light the unsurpassed, most brilliant torch of Dharma; you have been able to rain down the unsurpassed nectar-rain of Dharma; you have been able to sever the immeasurable enmities and fetters of affliction; you have been able to cause immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of beings to cross the shoreless and fearsome great ocean, to be liberated from the boundless cycle of birth and death, and to encounter immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Buddhas.”
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* can bring about various immeasurable merits in both the future and the present. Therefore, if a king of men should hear this subtle and wondrous sūtra, he will have already planted roots of goodness in the presence of hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of immeasurable Buddhas.”

Out of my reverence for this king of men, and because I perceive immeasurable merit and benefit therein, we—the four kings and our retinues of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of spirits—shall, upon seeing these various auspicious signs such as clouds of incense smoke and canopies of fragrance within our own palaces, conceal ourselves and remain invisible. For the sake of hearing the Dharma, we shall go to the palace where this king resides and to the place where the Dharma is being preached.

Mahābrahmā Deva-rāja, Śakra Devendra, Mahāprajñā Devī, Guṇakāra Devī, the Earth Goddess Dhṛtarāṣṭrā, the Spirit General Vaiśravaṇa, the Great General, and the great generals of the twenty-eight divisions of spirits; Maheśvara, Vajrapāṇi, the Spirit General Maṇibhadra, Hārītī with her five hundred sons—all surrounded him on every side. Furthermore, the Dragon Kings Anavatapta and Sāgara, along with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of spirits and devas, all came for the sake of hearing the Dharma; they each concealed themselves and did not manifest their bodies as they arrived at the palace where this human king resided and at the place where the Dharma was being preached.
“World-Honored One!

We, the four kings, along with our retinues and immeasurable spirits, shall all with one mind regard this king as a virtuous friend (kalyāṇamitra). We shall practice together in accordance with wholesome conduct, for he is a donor of the unsurpassed Great Dharma who satisfies us with the flavor of ambrosia.

We should protect this king, removing his misfortunes and afflictions so that he may attain peace and security; furthermore, we shall cause all evil calamities within his palace, kingdom, lands, and cities to be completely extinguished.”
“World-Honored One!
If there is a king who, regarding this sutra, gives rise to a mind of abandonment and takes no pleasure in hearing it; whose heart has no desire to revere, make offerings to, respect, or praise it;
and if among the fourfold assembly there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, or expound it, yet he likewise cannot revere, make offerings to, respect, or praise them.”

If we—the four kings, our retinues, and the immeasurable spirits—should fail to hear this True Dharma, we would turn away from the flavor of the Deathless, lose the great benefit of the Dharma, and be deprived of power and majesty; thus the hosts of devas would diminish while the evil realms increase.
“World-Honored One!
We four kings and immeasurable spirits will abandon that land; not only we, but also the immeasurable ancient virtuous deities who have long protected the land will all depart.”

Once we kings and all the spirits have departed, that land shall experience various calamities and portents; all the people will lose their virtuous minds, remaining only bound by anger and strife, destroying one another, and suffering from many epidemics. Comets and strange meteors shall appear and fall, the five planets and the lunar mansions shall deviate from their regular courses, two suns shall appear simultaneously, and the sun and moon shall undergo eclipses. White and black evil rainbows shall appear repeatedly; the earth shall quake and emit great sounds; violent winds and torrential rains shall occur almost daily; grain and rice shall become exceedingly expensive, leading to famine and starvation; many enemies and bandits from other regions shall invade and plunder the land, causing the people much suffering and distress, such that there will be no place in that land to find joy or delight.
“World-Honored One!

When we—the four kings, the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of spirits and ghosts, and the long-standing benevolent deities who protect the lands—depart from them, such immeasurable evil events as these will arise.”
“World-Honored One!

If there is a king who wishes to protect himself and his kingdom so that they may enjoy abundant peace and happiness; who wishes to cause all sentient beings within his realm to fully achieve and possess joy; who wishes to subdue all external enemies; who wishes to protect all territories; who wishes to govern his kingdom with the True Dharma; and who wishes to eliminate the fears of sentient beings.”
World-Honored One!
These kings of men and others should certainly listen to this sutra, and they should respectfully make offerings to those who read, recite, receive, and uphold this sutra.

We, the four kings and immeasurable spirits and deities, by means of these roots of goodness from this Dharma-food, shall partake of the unsurpassed flavor of the nectar of Dharma; our physical strength shall increase, our mental vigor shall become sharp and resolute, and we shall augment the power of all the devas.

Why is this? Because this king of men listens to and receives this sutra with a sincere heart, just as the various Brahmā devas expound discourses on the transcendence of desire, Śakra Devendra expounds various virtuous discourses, and those with the five supernatural powers expound the discourses of the rishis and immortals.
“World-Honored One!

Although Brahmā, Śakra Devendra, and those with the five supernormal powers may possess hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of immeasurable superior discourses, this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama* is the most supreme among them.”

Why is this? It is because the Tathāgata has preached this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* for the sake of sentient beings; to cause all kings of men within Jambudvīpa to rule by the True Dharma; to bestow peace and happiness upon all sentient beings; to desire to protect all sentient beings; to ensure that sentient beings are free from all suffering and affliction; to ensure they are without the thorns of enemies and bandits from other regions; to cause them to turn their backs on all evils rather than face them; and to ensure that the kingdom is free from anxiety and distress, where the True Dharma is taught so that there is no contention or litigation. Therefore, each king of men, within his own realm, should kindle the torch of the Dharma, blaze with the True Dharma, and increase the hosts of devas.

By these causes and conditions, we—the four kings, immeasurable spirits and ghosts, and all the celestial benevolent deities within Jambudvīpa—shall partake of the nectar-like flavor of the Dharma to our full satisfaction; we shall attain great majesty and virtue, and be endowed with vigor and strength. Within Jambudvīpa, there shall be peace, stability, abundance, and joy; the population shall flourish, and all shall dwell in happiness.

Furthermore, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of inconceivable nayutas of kalpas in future ages, we shall constantly experience the most subtle and supreme bliss, and we shall encounter immeasurable Buddhas to plant various roots of goodness, after which we shall realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

The attainment of such immeasurable merits as these is entirely taught by the Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. Because of the power of his great compassion, the Tathāgata surpasses hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Brahmās; and because of the power of his ascetic practices, he also surpasses immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Śakras.
Therefore, for the sake of all sentient beings, the Tathāgata has expounded this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*.

Whether it be all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa or the kings of men, whatever worldly or supramundane affairs of state they perform, and whatever secular treatises they compose, all arise from this sūtra.
In order to enable sentient beings to attain peace and happiness, Śākyamuni Tathāgata has manifested this sutra and caused it to be widely proclaimed and disseminated.
World-Honored One!
For these reasons, these kings of men ought certainly to listen to, receive, make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise this sutra.
At that time, the Buddha again addressed the Four Heavenly Kings:
"You Four Kings, along with your retinues— the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of spirits and deities—
if these human kings can listen to this sutra with a sincere heart, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising it;..."
"You Four Kings, you ought to protect them properly, extinguishing their misfortunes and afflictions while bestowing peace and happiness.

If there are those who can widely proclaim and disseminate such a sublime scripture, performing great Buddha-work among humans and devas and bringing great benefit to immeasurable sentient beings—such persons, you Four Kings, must certainly protect so that no external conditions may disturb them, allowing their minds to be tranquil and filled with joy, so that they may continue to widely proclaim this sutra."

At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, knelt with their right knees on the ground, and with palms joined before the World-Honored One, praised him in verse:
“The Buddha-moon is pure, Perfectly full and adorned; The Buddha-sun shines resplendent, Radiating a thousand rays of light.”
The face and eyes of the Tathāgata are most supreme, luminous, and pure; his teeth are white and stainless, like the roots of a lotus.
His merit is immeasurable, like the great ocean;
the abyss of his wisdom is boundless, fully endowed with the waters of the Dharma.
Possessing hundreds of thousands of samādhis without deficiency;
the soles of his feet are level and full, manifesting the mark of the thousand-spoked wheel;
his toes are joined by webbing, just like those of the king of geese.
His radiance shines brilliantly, like the king of jewel mountains;
subtle, wondrous, and pure, like refined, genuine gold;
all his merits and virtues are inconceivable.
To the mountain of the Buddha’s merit, I now pay homage.
Like space, he manifests forms in accordance with things;
like the moon in water, he is without obstruction; like a flame, like a transformation—therefore, I now...
"I prostrate to the Buddha-moon.
At that time, the World-Honored One replied in verse:
"This *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of all sutras, is most profound and supreme."
It is unsurpassed;
it has been proclaimed by the World-Honored One endowed with the Ten Powers, and you, O Four Kings, should protect it with diligence.
This profound and wondrous scripture can bestow immeasurable happiness upon sentient beings;
for the sake of the peace, happiness, and benefit of all beings, it shall circulate for a long time within Jambudvīpa.
They can extinguish all the evil realms and immeasurable sufferings within the three thousandfold great thousandfold world system.
If various kings of men give rise to a heart of compassion and govern the world with the True Dharma,
