and if they are able to propagate this wondrous sutra, then their lands—
Peaceful and abundant, may all sentient beings therein experience every form of happiness.
If there is a king who desires to cherish his own person, as well as his kingdom,
and wishes for them to be prosperous, he should with a sincere heart bathe himself until pure and clean.
Go to the place of the Dharma assembly to hear and receive this sutra.
This sutra can bring about all virtuous deeds and subdue all internal and external enemies;
furthermore, it can eliminate immeasurable fears.
These kings of sutras can bestow peace, security, and happiness upon all immeasurable sentient beings.
They are like a jewel tree standing within a person’s home, which is able to produce every kind of precious treasure.
This sublime sūtra is likewise so; it is able to give birth to all the merits of kings.
Just as clear, cool water can eliminate thirst and exhaustion;
this sublime sūtra is likewise so, able to eliminate the thirst for merit among kings.
Just as a casket containing rare jewels and extraordinary objects is held entirely in one's hand to be used as one pleases;
so too is this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, which can, according to one's will,
bestow the Dharma-jewels upon all kings.
This *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, this subtle and wondrous sūtra, is constantly revered and made offerings to by the various devas;
it is also protected and sustained by the majestic power and authority of the Four Great Kings, the World-Protectors.
The Buddhas of the ten directions always keep this sūtra in mind; if there should be anyone who expounds it, [they shall likewise protect them].
They praised him, saying, "Excellent!
Furthermore, hundreds of thousands of immeasurable spirits and deities came from the ten directions to protect this person;
if anyone should hear this wondrous sutra, their hearts will give rise to joy, leaping for immeasurable delight.
Within Jambudvīpa, immeasurable multitudes are all filled with joy as they assemble to hear this sutra;
by hearing this sutra, they possess all majestic virtues, and the celestial hosts increase in vital essence and physical strength.
At that time, having heard these verses, the Four Heavenly Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Since long ago, we have never before heard such a subtle and wondrous Dharma of quiescent extinction. Having heard this, our hearts were filled with both sorrow and joy; tears flowed down our cheeks, our entire bodies trembled, and our limbs relaxed with ease. Furthermore, we attained immeasurable, inconceivable, and perfect sublime bliss.”
With celestial *mandārava* flowers and *mahāmandārava* flowers, they made offerings by scattering them over the Tathāgata.
Having thus performed such offerings to the Buddha, they again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
"We Four Kings each have five hundred spirits and deities who shall constantly follow and protect this preacher of the Dharma.
Chapter Seven: The Great Eloquence Deity (*Mahāpratisarā-devī*) At that time, the Great Eloquence Deity addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One! [I too shall protect such preachers]."

I shall augment the eloquence of this Dharma-preacher, causing his discourse to be adorned with sequential order and to excellently attain great wisdom. If there are errors in this sutra regarding characters, phrases, meanings, or contradictions, I can cause this bhikṣu who preaches the Dharma to recover them in their proper sequence and grant him dhāraṇī so that he may not forget them.

If there are sentient beings who have planted various roots of goodness under hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, for their sake, this Dharma-preacher shall widely proclaim and disseminate this sublime sūtra throughout Jambudvīpa so that it may not be interrupted. Furthermore, he shall cause immeasurable and boundless sentient beings to hear this sūtra, so that they may all attain a fierce and sharp, inconceivable mass of great wisdom; they shall receive the retribution of immeasurable merit; they shall skillfully understand infinite varieties of expedient means; they shall be adept at eloquently expounding all treatises; they shall be well-versed in the various arts and crafts of the world; they shall be able to transcend birth and death and attain the stage of non-retrogression; and they shall certainly and swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Chapter Eight: The Chapter on Śrīdevī. At that time, Śrīdevī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

As for this Dharma-preacher, I shall provide him with whatever he requires—clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and other assets—supplying this person so that nothing is lacking, enabling his mind to abide in peace and joy day and night, as he reflects with right mindfulness upon the chapters and verses of this sutra and discerns its profound meaning.

If there are sentient beings who have planted various roots of goodness under hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, for their sake this Dharma-preacher shall widely proclaim and disseminate this sublime sūtra throughout Jambudvīpa so that it may not be interrupted. “World-Honored One!

I have already planted various roots of goodness in the past under the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, World-Honored One named Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakaparvata-prabhāsa. If there is anyone who can recite this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* to make offerings to me and to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; and if, having recited my name three times, they burn incense as an offering;

and having made offerings to the Buddhas, they further present various fragrant flowers and exquisite delicacies to me, scattering them in all directions—know that such a person will be able to gather wealth, resources, and treasures.

By these causes and conditions, the essence of the earth increases; the earth deities and all the devas are filled with joy. The sprouts, stalks, branches, leaves, and fruits of the sown grains flourish and grow lushly, and the tree deities rejoice as they produce immeasurable varieties of things.
"At that time, out of my compassionate concern for all sentient beings, I provided them with many necessities of life.
World-Honored One!

To the north of here, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa has a city named Aṇimandita. Within that city is a park named Puṇyapuṣpābhāsa; in this park is a most excellent garden called Suvarṇadhvaja, made of the seven precious jewels and exceedingly wonderful—this is my constant place of residence."

If there is anyone who wishes to increase their wealth and treasures, that person should, within their own dwelling, sweep and sprinkle it clean, bathe their body, put on fresh white garments, and anoint themselves with exquisite incense. For my sake, they should sincerely recite the name of that Buddha, the World-Honored One Ratnakusuma-vaidūrya, three times, prostrating, making offerings, burning incense, and scattering flowers;

they should also recite the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* three times and make a vow with utmost sincerity. Furthermore, using fragrant flowers and various delicious foods, they should offer them to me and scatter them in all directions, at which time they should recite these verses:

“Pāripūṇṇacāri, samantadharṣaṇīrākṣa, mahāvihāragati, samantavidhānagati, mahākālipati, pabade, sarvadhve, samanta, suparipūrṇe, ajñādharmate, mahāvidyubhite, mahāmaitreyasaṃgīte, hite śiśibodhihite, samantāstha, anuparane. This consecration mantra-phrase is certainly auspicious, true, and not false.”

Sentient beings of equal practice who possess middling roots of goodness should uphold, recite, and master this [sūtra]. For seven days and seven nights, they should observe the eight precepts, purify their minds morning and evening, and make offerings of incense and flowers to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Constantly, for the sake of themselves and all sentient beings, they should dedicate their merit toward the fulfillment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, making this vow:
"May all that I seek attain auspiciousness."
He shall personally clean and sweep the dwelling or house where he resides.

Whether it be his own residence or a forest hermitage (āraṇya), he shall smear the ground with fragrant clay, burn exquisite incense, and arrange pure and fine seats. He shall scatter various flowers and perfumes upon the ground to await me;

at that moment, in the space of a single thought, I shall enter his abode and sit upon that seat. From that day and night forth, I shall cause this dwelling—whether it be a village, a monastery, or an open space—to lack for nothing: whether it be money, gold and silver, precious gems, cattle and sheep, or grain and rice; everything required shall be fully provided, and all shall experience happiness.

If you can dedicate the most excellent portion of the roots of goodness you have cultivated to me, I shall never distance myself from that person for the rest of my life; wherever they dwell, I will protect and mind them with a sincere heart, and I will cause whatever they seek to be accomplished.
"You should, with a sincere heart, pay homage to these various Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, whose names are as follows:

and the Bodhisattva Dharmodgata; as well as to the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the east, the Tathāgata Ratnaketu of the south, the Buddha Amitāyus of the west, and the Buddha Sutejoghoṣa of the north.
Chapter Nine: The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā (2). The *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Chapter Nine: The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā. At that time, the Earth Goddess Sthāvarā addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

This subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* Sūtra, whether in the present world or in future worlds, wherever it may be—whether in cities or villages, in mountains or marshes, in desolate places, or in royal palaces and residences.
"Blessed One!
Wherever this sutra is circulated, I shall arrange lion thrones within that region and cause the preachers of the Dharma to sit upon them to extensively expound and proclaim this wondrous sutra.
I shall constantly provide protective service therein, concealing my body beneath the Dharma throne and supporting their feet with my head."

Having heard the Dharma, I have partaken of the supreme flavor of the nectar-like Dharma, which increases my physical strength; furthermore, this great earth—extending sixteen hundred and eighty thousand yojanas from the vajra-limit up to the surface of the ocean—has obtained a full abundance of various flavors and has become more fertile, rich, and lush than it was today.

For this reason, within Jambudvīpa, medicinal herbs, trees, roots, stalks, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits flourish and grow luxuriantly, fully endowed with beautiful color, fragrance, and flavor.

Once sentient beings have eaten, their lifespan, physical form, strength, eloquence, and tranquility increase; their six sense faculties become fully developed and sharp; and their majesty and countenances become upright, dignified, and extraordinary.
Having accomplished these various qualities, they are largely successful in the tasks they undertake, possessing great power, diligence, and valor.
"Therefore, World-Honored One!

Within Jambudvīpa, there will be peace, security, abundance, and joy, and the population will flourish; all sentient beings will experience much happiness, with their minds satisfied and their wishes fulfilled according to their desires."

Once these sentient beings have attained such majestic power and great influence, they will be able to make offerings to this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra*, as well as to the fourfold assembly who uphold this sūtra, honoring and making offerings to them.
At that time, I shall go to that place; for the sake of causing all sentient beings to experience happiness, I shall request the Dharma-preacher to extensively proclaim such a sublime scripture.
For what reason?
World-Honored One!

When this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* is expounded in detail, the merit obtained by myself and my retinue shall be twice that of usual times; our physical strength will increase, and our minds will become more vigorous and resolute.
“World-Honored One!
Having partaken of the unsurpassed flavor of ambrosia, the land of Jambudvīpa, measuring seven thousand yojanas in length and breadth, has become twice as fertile as usual.
World-Honored One!”

In this way, the great earth is the support for all sentient beings and is able to increase all things required by them. Therefore, World-Honored One!
These sentient beings, in order to repay my kindness, should form this thought:

"We have now heard this most profound and unsurpassed sublime Dharma; we have already grasped an inconceivable mass of merit and encountered immeasurable and boundless Buddhas. "Each of these sentient beings, while in their respective dwellings, may expound this sutra for others—whether explaining a single parable, a single chapter, or a single causal narrative; or further, praising a single Buddha, a single bodhisattva, a single four-line verse, or even a single phrase; or even merely reciting the title of this sutra."
World-Honored One!

Wherever these sentient beings dwell, that land shall be endowed with rich, fertile soil far surpassing other lands; whatever grows from the ground there shall all increase, flourish, and expand, causing all sentient beings to experience happiness, to abound in wealth and treasures, to delight in practicing generosity, and to have minds that are always firm and deeply faithful in the Triple Gem.

Earth Deity!

If there are sentient beings who, for the sake of making offerings to this sutra, adorn their dwellings—even by hanging up a single banner, a single parasol, or a single garment—then upon the end of their lives, they will be reborn in the natural palaces of the seven treasures that exist among the six heavens of the desire realm.
"O Earth Deity!

11. Chapter on Right Discourse (3). *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Chapter Eleven: The Chapter on Right Discourse. At that time, the Buddha addressed the earth goddess Dṛḍhā:

brothers and sisters, kinsmen and wives are scattered and driven into exile, and his own body likewise perishes.
Meteors fall in great numbers, and two suns appear simultaneously;
evil bandits from other regions invade and plunder the land;
the people suffer from hunger, and there are many pestilential diseases.

and the flavor of grains, fruits, and all produce diminishes.

those who practice goodness shall attain birth among the heavens.

Maṇikaṇṭha, as well as Nirgrantha, the Great Rain-Master deity,
the Great Food-and-Drink deity, Mahāgaṭa, the Suvarṇakeśa deity, the Bhṛṅgin spirit, as well as the Piṅgala and Carpaṭa spirits.
Possessing great majesty and power are the god Pāṇali, Dharmabhadra, Makhabhadra, the Kīṭakeśa spirit, Śūramitra, Renukeśa, Mahāpāṇa, as well as Skandha.
Khaṇḍaśāṭī, and furthermore the great deity Śarabhaṇḍī, Hemavata, Satākīrti, Dakṣapaṇī, Āgavara, Cīramāja, and Aṅgulimāla.
Such spirits as these, all infinite in number, possessing great power and supernatural faculties,
shall constantly and diligently provide protection for those who hear and receive this subtle and wondrous sutra.
The Dragon King Anavatapta, the King Sāgara, the King Mucilinda,
the King Elāpattra, the Dragon King Nanda, and the King Upananda— such as these,
hundreds of thousands of dragon kings, with their great supernormal powers, [gathered there].
They shall constantly come to protect those who listen to this sutra, never departing from them day or night.
Pāli-raho, the asura king; Vemacitra, as well as Kharaskandha, Śambara, and Prahasta—
Kharaskandha and Gandhara— these are all asura kings who possess great supernormal powers;
they constantly come to protect those who listen to this sutra, never leaving them by day or night.
The Mother of Demons and her five hundred spirits will constantly come to protect those who listen to this sutra, whether they are asleep or awake.
The great spirits and deities, the women and the Kūṣmāṇḍas, and the Kūṣmāṇḍīs who devour the vital essence of humans— such spirits as these, all possessing great power,
shall constantly and diligently protect those throughout the worlds of the ten directions who receive and uphold this sutra.
Mahāprajñāpāramitā-devī and the other immeasurable goddesses, as well as Śrī-devī and her respective retinues, the Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā,
and the great deities of planting groves and bearing fruit— may all such deities give rise to joy in their hearts.
They shall all come to protect, cherish, and draw near to those who uphold this sutra.
For all sentient beings, they shall increase their lifespan, physical appearance, and strength; their merit, majesty, and countenance shall be twice as magnificent as usual.
The five planets and all the lunar mansions, their transformations, anomalies, and calamitous portents—all these can be extinguished without exception;
even the evil dreams seen while lying down at night, which cause distress and emaciation upon waking—such evil matters as these shall all be utterly extinguished.
The earth deity possesses great power, and its domain is exceedingly profound; by the power of this sutra, it can transform its flavor.
At a thickness of one hundred and sixty-eight thousand yojanas, the essence and flavor within it—
There is nowhere it does not pervade; it causes [the essence] to well up everywhere, nourishing and benefiting sentient beings.

By the power of this sutra, it is able to cause the "earth-essence" (pṛthivī-rasa) to emerge entirely above the ground to a thickness of one hundred yojanas, and it also enables the various devas to obtain abundant vital energy.
Physical strength is replenished and increased, and there is joy and happiness.
All the deities within Jambudvīpa give rise to joy in their hearts and experience immeasurable bliss;
by the power of this sutra, the various devas rejoice, and the hundred grains and all fruits flourish.
All things flourish and thrive; the gardens and groves, with their thickets and forests, have their flowers in full bloom, their fragrances exquisite and pervasive, filling and suffusing everywhere.
All the hundred grasses, trees, and shrubs grow upright and straight; their forms are supple and soft, without any crookedness or distortion.
Within Jambudvīpa, all the dragon maidens, numbering immeasurably and beyond thought,
gave rise to joy in their hearts; leaping for joy beyond measure,
they adorned flower ponds in every place, and within those ponds—
Various kinds of flowers were born: the utpala, the padma, the kumuda, and the puṇḍarīka;
all clouds and mists were cleared away, so that within the void there was no longer any dust or obscuration.
All directions are clear and transparent, pure, clean, and luminous;
the Sun-King blazes with fierce flames, emitting a thousand rays of light, leaping for joy as he illuminates all obscurations and darkness.
With Jāmbūnada gold, they have fashioned palaces; dwelling therein, their majestic virtue is immeasurable.
The Son of Heaven, the Sun, and the Deity, the Moon, because they hear this sutra, are filled with vital essence.
Emerging from Jambudvīpa, his heart filled with joy, he emitted immeasurable nets of brilliant light that illuminated all directions;
at the very moment of his emergence, he radiated a great web of light, causing the various lotus flowers in all the ponds to bloom.
Within Jambudvīpa, immeasurable fruits ripen in their seasons,
satisfying all sentient beings.
At that time, the illumination of the sun and moon is particularly sublime.
The constellations move in their proper courses, not failing their appointed measures;
wind and rain come in their seasons, bringing abundant and flourishing harvests;
there is an abundance of wealth and treasures, with nothing lacking.
Wherever this subtle and wondrous scripture, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, is circulated and recited,
that land and its realm shall immediately obtain the increase of the immeasurable merits as described above.

Chapter 14: The Bestowal of Prophecy (3). *The Golden Light Sūtra*, Chapter Fourteen: The Bestowal of Prophecy. At that time, the Tathāgata was about to bestow the prophecy of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa and his two sons, Rajalakṣaṇa and Rajaprabha.

At that time, there were ten thousand devaputras, with King Blazing Majesty as their leader, who all came together from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to the place where the Buddha was; they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa:

"In a future age, after immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of incalculable nayutas of kalpas have passed, in the world-system called Suvarṇāvabhāsa, you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Suvarṇaratnacchatraśikhara-rāja."

Furthermore, after this Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, and once both the True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma have completely vanished, the eldest son, Rajatākṣa, shall succeed him as the Buddha in that realm. At that time, the world will be renamed Viśuddhadhvaja, and the Buddha will be named Jambūnadasuvarṇadhvajaprabhāsasamantāvabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.

Until after this Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, and when both the True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma have completely vanished, his younger son, Silver Light, shall succeed him in the position of Buddha. The name of the world shall remain as it was before, without change; the Buddha shall be known as Golden Radiance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.

When these ten thousand devaputras heard that the three great bodhisattvas had received their predictions of enlightenment, and further heard this *Suvarṇabhāsottama-sūtra*, they were filled with joy and gave rise to a heart of profound reverence. Their minds became free from defilement and entanglement like pure lapis lazuli; they were pure and unimpeded, just like space.
At that time, the Tathāgata, knowing that the roots of goodness of these ten thousand devaputras had matured, immediately bestowed upon them the prediction of their attainment of the path to bodhi:
"O you devaputras!..."

In a future age, after passing through incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas, they shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in this world. They shall all belong to the same family, the same clan, and the same name, being called the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān named Nīlanetra-utpala-gandha-kūṭa. Appearing in the world in such succession, there shall be ten thousand Buddhas in total.
At that time, the tree deity of the site of enlightenment named Samudgata addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

These ten thousand devaputras have come to this assembly from the palace of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven for the sake of hearing the Dharma; why has the Tathāgata immediately bestowed predictions of their future enlightenment upon them?”

"Bhagavān! I have never before heard that these sons of the gods have fully practiced the six pāramitās; nor have I ever heard that they have given away their hands, feet, heads, eyes, marrow, and brains, nor their beloved wives and children, wealth, treasures, grain, and silks; nor gold, silver, lapis lazuli, tridacna shells, agate, coral, conch shells, jade, and precious stones; nor delicious foods, drinks, clothing, bedding, medicines for the sick, elephants, horses, and carriages; nor palaces, houses, gardens, groves, springs, and ponds; nor slaves and servants—just as other immeasurable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas have done by respectfully making offerings with various requisites for life to the past immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Buddha-Bhagavāns."

In this way, in future ages, these bodhisattvas will likewise relinquish immeasurable things held dear—heads, eyes, marrow, and brains, as well as beloved wives, children, wealth, treasures, grain, silks, and even servants—practicing in succession until they fully accomplish the six pāramitās. Having accomplished these, they will further cultivate ascetic practices for immeasurable and boundless kalpas, only after which they shall receive the prediction of enlightenment (bodhi-vyākaraṇa).
World-Honored One!

For what cause and by what condition have these sons of heaven cultivated such supreme and wondrous roots of goodness that, having come from that celestial realm, they were able to hear the Dharma briefly and immediately receive their prediction of enlightenment?
“I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for me and sever the net of my doubts.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the tree deity: “O Good Goddess!
All have causes and conditions, and possess wondrous roots of goodness, practicing according to their respective characteristics. Why is this?

Because these sons of heaven have renounced the pleasures of the five desires in their respective abodes and have come to listen to this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra*. Having heard the Dharma, they maintain a pure and reverent mind toward this sutra and practice according to its teachings. Furthermore, having heard that these three great bodhisattvas have received their predictions (*vyākaraṇa*), and by virtue of the causes and conditions of their original vows made in the past, I now bestow predictions upon them all, that in a future age they shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Chapter 15: Eliminating Disease (3). In the *Suvarṇabhāsottama-sūtra*, Chapter Fifteen, "Eliminating Disease," the Buddha addressed the Bodhi-tree goddess of the site of enlightenment:
"O Good Goddess!"
Listen attentively, listen attentively!
Retain this well in your memory; I shall expound for you the causes and conditions of my past vows.

In the past, immeasurable, inconceivable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there appeared in the world a Buddha named Ratnaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
“Good Woman Devī!

At that time, after this Buddha had entered parinirvāṇa and the True Dharma (saddharma) had ceased, during the period of the Semblance Dharma (pratirūpakadharma), there was a king named Devendraprabha-rāja. He practiced the True Dharma and ruled the world according to the law; the people were harmonious and submissive, filially supporting their parents.”

In this king’s realm, there was an elder named Jālinīprabha who was skilled in medical arts and saved others from the suffering of illness; he was adept at skillful means for discerning the increase and decrease of the four great elements.
"O Good Goddess!

At that time, a son was born later into the household of the Elder Jālinīprabha, named Jalavāhana. His physical appearance was exceptionally superior and most handsome; his form and color were subtle and wondrous, and he was endowed with majestic virtue. By nature he was intelligent and quick-witted, well-versed in all treatises, and there was no skill, art, writing, calculation, or accounting that he did not master."

At that time, a pestilence descended upon the kingdom, and there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings who could not escape it, all of them tormented by various sufferings and afflictions.

“Good Goddess! At that time, the elder’s son Flowing Water, seeing these immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings undergoing various sufferings and afflictions, gave rise to great compassion for them and reflected thus:
‘These immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings are undergoing various sufferings and afflictions.’”

"My father, the elder, though skilled in medicine and capable of saving others from all suffering, being adept at understanding through skillful means the increase and decrease of the four great elements, has now reached an advanced age; he is decrepit, withered, and frail, his skin is loose, his face is wrinkled, and he is emaciated and trembling. In coming and going, he must rely on a cane and a staff; exhausted and weary, he cannot reach those cities and villages.

Yet these immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings have encountered grave illnesses for which there is no one to save them. I shall now go to my father, the great physician, to inquire about the secret methods of medical prescriptions for treating disease. Having received this instruction and gained this knowledge, I shall go to the cities, villages, and hamlets to treat the various grave illnesses of all sentient beings, causing them all to be liberated from immeasurable sufferings."

Then, having reflected thus, the son of the householder went to his father’s place, prostrated himself with his head to the ground, paid homage to his father, and stood back with palms joined. He questioned his father regarding the increase and decrease of the four great elements, and immediately spoke this verse:
"How should one know when the four great elements and the various faculties decline, undergo transformation, and give rise to all manner of illnesses?"
How should one know the proper timing for food and drink, so that after eating, the bodily fire does not diminish?
How should one know the treatment for disorders of wind, heat, water, spleen disease, and those of equal proportions?
"When does the wind move? When does the heat move? When does the water move, so as to harm sentient beings?
Then the father, the elder, immediately answered his son with a verse, explaining the medical prescriptions:
Three months are autumn, three months are winter, and three months are spring;
these constitute the twelve months, explained in groups of three.
From such reckonings, there are four seasons in a year;
if expressed in pairs, they comprise six periods; when subsumed in threes, they are three fundamental divisions;
and when expressed in twos, they are the manifest seasons. According to these seasonal divisions, [the following applies].
Regulating one’s food and drink can benefit the body; however,
throughout the course of the seasons and years, the various faculties and the four great elements undergo cycles of transformation, increase, and decrease,
causing the body to fall ill.
In the third month, one should provide nourishment, harmonizing the six elements through diet and medicinal decoctions according to the specific ailment.
For those with a predominance of wind disorders, these afflictions flare up during the summer.
Those with feverish diseases manifest in autumn;
those with diseases of balanced humors manifest in winter;
and those with lung diseases intensify in spring.
Those with wind disorders (*vāta*) should consume fatty, salty, sour, and hot foods during the summer;
those with heat disorders (*pitta*) should consume cold and sweet foods in autumn; and in winter, they should consume a balanced mixture of sweet, sour, and fatty foods.
For lung diseases, one should consume fatty, pungent, and hot foods during the spring.
If one eats to satiety and then [engages in strenuous activity], lung disease will manifest;
when the food is being digested, feverish illness will manifest.
After food has been digested, wind disorders arise.
Thus, these four great elements manifest according to the three seasons: when wind disorders cause emaciation, one should supplement with ghee and fatty substances;
for heat disorders, administer purgatives and take harītakī.
For diseases such as these, one should take three kinds of excellent medicines: namely, those that are sweet and pungent, as well as those that are oily with clarified butter;
for lung diseases, one should take emetics according to one's capacity.
"If one acts contrary to the proper time, one should rely upon the teacher to deliberate and provide food,
drink, and medicinal decoctions according to the illness. "O Goddess of Goodness!"

At that time, the elder’s son, Flowing Water, questioned his father, the physician, regarding the increase and decrease of the four great elements; through this, he mastered all medical prescriptions.

Having acquired knowledge of these prescriptions, the elder’s son traveled throughout the cities, towns, and villages within the kingdom, and wherever there were those suffering from the ailments of sentient beings, he would comfort them with gentle words, saying:
"I am a physician, I am a physician. I am well-versed in prescriptions and medicines; I shall now treat and provide relief for you, so that you may all be completely healed."

“Good Woman Devī! At that time, when the sentient beings heard the elder’s son speak words of gentle consolation and grant his promise to treat their illnesses, their hearts were filled with immeasurable joy and they leaped for joy beyond measure.”

At that time, there were hundreds of thousands of immeasurable sentient beings who had contracted extremely grave illnesses; upon merely hearing these words, their hearts were filled with joy, and all manner of ailments were immediately cured, restored to their original state, and their vital energy became fully replenished.

“Good Goddess! Furthermore, there were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings whose illnesses were so deep and grave that they were difficult to cure. They all came together to the place where the son of the elder was; at that time, the son of the elder immediately gave them excellent medicine and had them take it. Having taken it, their illnesses were eliminated and they were restored to health.”
"O Good Goddess! This son of a householder has completely cured all the sufferings of illness among the sentient beings within his kingdom.
— *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, Scroll Three.
The Golden Light Sūtra, Scroll Four, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Sixteen: The Elder’s Son Jalavāhana (4). The Golden Light Sūtra, Chapter Sixteen: The Elder’s Son Jalavāhana.
The Buddha told the tree deity:

"At that time, after the Elder’s Son Flowing Water had healed the immeasurable sufferings and ailments of all sentient beings within the realm of King Sovereign Light of Heaven, he restored their bodies to their original state so that they might enjoy various pleasures.
Because their illnesses were cured, they performed many meritorious deeds and practiced generosity; they honored and revered this Elder’s Son, speaking thus:"
"Excellent, householder!

You are able to greatly increase the accumulation of merit and bestow immeasurable life upon sentient beings. You are truly a great king of physicians, skillfully treating the immeasurable grave illnesses of sentient beings; you must surely be a bodhisattva well-versed in prescriptions and medicines."
“Good Woman Devī! At that time, the elder’s son had a wife named Water-Empty Dragon-Treasury (Śūnyatā-jala-nāga-kośa), who gave birth to two sons:
the first was named Water-Empty (Jala-śūnya), and the second was named Water-Treasury (Jala-kośa).”

At that time, the elder’s son took these two children and traveled in succession through cities and villages until they finally reached a vast, desolate marsh. There he saw tigers, wolves, foxes, dogs, birds, and beasts, all of whom were devouring flesh and blood and were fleeing away in one direction.
At that time, the son of the elder had this thought:
"For what cause and condition are these birds and beasts running away in one direction?
I should follow after them and observe."

Then the son of the elder followed after him and saw a pond whose water had dried up; within that pond there were many fish. Upon seeing these fish, the son of the elder gave rise to a heart of great compassion.
At that time, a tree spirit manifested half of her body and spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent! O great son of good family!"
"These fish are pitiable; you should give them water, and for this reason you shall be named Flowing Water (Śrotasvā).
Furthermore, there are two reasons for the name 'Flowing Water':
first, the ability to cause water to flow, and second, the ability to bestow water."
"You should now determine the reality according to the name.
Then the son of the elder asked the tree deity,
"How many fish heads are there in total?"
The tree deity replied:
"Their number is exactly ten thousand, complete and full.
"O Good Goddess! [the Buddha continued.]
At that time, having heard these numbers, the Flowing Water [King] felt his great compassion increase all the more.
"O Good Goddess!

At that time, this empty pond was scorched by the sun until only a small amount of water remained; those ten thousand fish were on the verge of death. They writhed about in all four directions, and seeing this elder, they conceived a sense of reliance upon him. Following the direction in which the elder went, they pursued and gazed after him, their eyes never once leaving him."

At that time, the elder ran in all four directions, searching and seeking water but was unable to find any at all; he then looked around and saw a large tree, from which he immediately took branches and leaves and returned to the pond to provide shade and coolness.
Having created the shade, he further investigated where the water in this pool originally came from.
He went out in the four directions, searching everywhere, but could not find the source of the water. He then ran swiftly to another distant place and saw a great river named Jalamudbhava.
At that time, there were yet other wicked men who, for the sake of catching these fish, dammed up the water at a steep and perilous point upstream so that it could not flow downstream.

However, because the dammed spot was steep and dangerous, it would take ninety days to repair it even with the labor of hundreds of thousands of people; how much more difficult would it be for me alone?

Then the son of the elder quickly returned to the place where the great king was, prostrated with his head at the king’s feet, and withdrew to stand to one side. Joining his palms toward the king, he explained the circumstances and spoke these words:

“For the sake of the people in the kingdom of the Great King, I have been treating various ailments. As I traveled by stages, I arrived at that desolate marsh and saw a pond whose water had dried up. There were ten thousand fish being scorched by the sun; today they are in dire distress and will soon die.”
"I only pray that Your Majesty will lend me twenty great elephants so that I may carry water to save the lives of those fish, just as I have preserved the lives of these sick people.
Thereupon, the Great King immediately commanded his ministers to provide them with prompt assistance.
At that time, the minister, having received the king’s command, said to the elder:
"Excellent, Great Being!
You may now go yourself to the elephant stable and select as you please, so as to benefit sentient beings and enable them to attain happiness."

At that time, Flowing Water and his two sons took twenty large elephants and borrowed leather bags from the city builders. They quickly went to the breach in the upper reaches of the river, filled them with water, and carried it back on their backs at a rapid pace to the empty marsh pond. They lowered the bags from the elephants' backs and poured the water into the pond; thus, the water was completely replenished, returning to its former state.
At that time, the son of the elder paced back and forth along the four sides of the pond; the fish likewise followed him, moving along the bank.
Then the son of the elder thought to himself:
"For what reason does this fish follow me?"
"These fish must be tormented by the fire of hunger and wish to seek food and drink from me;
I shall now give it to them. "Good Woman Devī!
At that time, the Elder’s son, Flowing Water, said to his sons:"
"Take one of the elephants of greatest strength and go quickly to your home to inform your father, the elder:

'Gather all the edible things in the house—even the portions for your parents' consumption and those for your wife, children, and servants—and load them all onto the elephant; return with the utmost speed.'"
Then the two sons, following their father’s instructions, mounted the largest elephant and went to their home. They informed their grandfather of the aforementioned matters.
At that time, the two sons gathered all the edible items from the house, loaded them onto the back of the elephant, and quickly returned to their father at the empty marsh and pond.

At that time, the elder’s son, seeing his son return, felt immeasurable joy and exultation. He took food and drink from his son and scattered it into the pond; having fed the fish, he reflected to himself:
"I have now been able to provide these fish with food so that they are satiated; in future ages, I shall bestow upon them the food of the Dharma."
He further reflected:

"I have heard that in the past, in a secluded place, there was a bhikṣu who recited the Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras. Those sūtras state that if sentient beings, at the time of their death, hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, they will immediately be reborn in the heavens. I should now explain the profound Twelve Links of Dependent Origination for these ten thousand fish, and I shall also invoke the name of the Buddha Ratnasaṃbhava."
“At that time, there were two kinds of people in Jambudvīpa:
first, those who had deep faith in the Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras; second, those who reviled them and did not give rise to faith or joy.”
Then the son of the elder thought to himself:
"I shall now enter the waters of this pond and preach the profound and wondrous Dharma for these fish.
Having reflected thus, he immediately entered the water and spoke these words:
"Homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, the Jewel-Winnower of the Past."
In the past, when the Tathāgata Ratnavijaya was practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this vow:
"If there are sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions who hear my name at the time of their death, may they, immediately upon passing away, be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."

At that time, Flowing Water further expounded this profound and wondrous Dharma for the sake of these fish—namely: ignorance conditions volitional formations; volitional formations condition consciousness; consciousness conditions name-and-form; name-and-form conditions the six sense bases; the six sense bases condition contact; contact conditions feeling; feeling conditions craving; craving conditions clinging; clinging conditions existence; existence conditions birth; and birth conditions old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and despair.
“Good Goddess! At that time, the Elder’s son Flowing Water and his two sons, having preached this Dharma, returned home together.
Later, on another occasion, the Elder’s son was reclining, intoxicated from a gathering of guests.”
At that time, the earth suddenly shook violently; ten thousand fish died on the same day, and having died, they were reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
Once reborn in heaven, they reflected:
"By what causes and conditions of wholesome karma have we been born here in this Trāyastriṃśa Heaven?"
They further said to one another:

"Previously, within Jambudvīpa, we fell among the animals and took birth as fish. The Elder’s Son Flowing Water gave us water and food, and further explained for us the profound Twelve Links of Dependent Origination, while also invoking the name of the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava. By these causes and conditions, we have been enabled to be born in this heaven."
"Therefore, we should now go to the place where the son of the elder is, to repay his kindness and make offerings.
At that time, ten thousand devaputras descended from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to Jambudvīpa and arrived at the house of the great physician, the son of the elder, Śrotas.
At that time, the son of the elder was sleeping while lying on his back upon the open roof of the upper story.

These ten thousand devaputras placed ten thousand exquisite celestial pearl necklaces at the head of his bed; they placed another ten thousand at his feet; another ten thousand at his right side; and another ten thousand at his left side.
They rained down *māndārava* flowers and *mahāmāndārava* flowers, which accumulated up to his knees.
Various celestial musical instruments were played, producing exquisite sounds.
All those in Jambudvīpa who were asleep were awakened, and the Elder’s son, Flowing Water, likewise awoke from his sleep.

These ten thousand devaputras flew and roamed through the air above, raining down exquisite celestial lotuses everywhere throughout the kingdom of King Devendraprabha. These devaputras then returned to their original location at the pond in the wilderness and rained down celestial flowers once more; they subsequently vanished from that place and returned to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, where they enjoyed the five celestial sensual pleasures with complete ease and sovereignty as they pleased.
Then, when this night had passed in Jambudvīpa, King Devendraprabha asked his various ministers:
"For what reason did such pure and wondrous auspicious signs, accompanied by great radiance, appear last night?"
The minister replied, "Great King,

his virtue is like the sun, manifest and brilliant as it dwells in the sky.
Whirling to the right in a graceful turn, light flows forth;
like a lapis lazuli bead, its color is subtle and wondrous, like the sun situated in the sky.
At that time, the tree deity of the Bodhimaṇḍa further spoke this hymn of praise:

“Homage to the Pure One, the Unsurpassed Perfectly Awakened One! To the most profound and wondrous Dharma, which is realized through accordance with reality, and which is far removed from all that is non-Dharma and non-path.”
Emerging alone and preeminent, he attained the perfect enlightenment of a Buddha.
Knowing that existence is non-existence, his fundamental nature is pure; rare, how rare are the merits of the Tathāgata!
Rare, how rare is the great ocean of the Tathāgata!
Rare, rare, like Mount Sumeru; rare, rare, are the Buddha’s boundless practices;
rare, rare, is the Buddha’s appearance in the world, like the udumbara flower.
Appearing but once in an age;
rare is the Tathāgata, with immeasurable great compassion.
Śākyamuni, the sun among men, for the sake of benefiting [beings],...
For the sake of all sentient beings, you have proclaimed such a sublime and precious sūtra.
Excellent, O Tathāgata! With your faculties stilled, you have entered the great city of sublime tranquility.
Stainless and pure, this profound samādhi enters the sphere traversed by all Buddhas;
the bodies of all śrāvakas are entirely empty and quiescent, and the sphere traversed by the Two-legged World-Honored One is likewise empty.
All such things, these immeasurable dharmas, when their fundamental nature and characteristics are examined,
are likewise empty and quiescent;
the nature and characteristics of all sentient beings are also empty, yet because of their deluded and ignorant minds, they are unable to realize this.
I constantly mind the Buddha and delight in seeing the World-Honored One; I always make this vow never to be separated from the Buddha-sun.
Constantly upon the ground, I kneel long with palms joined, my heart full of longing and devotion, desiring to see the Buddha.
I constantly practice the supreme great compassion, weeping and shedding tears as rain, desiring to see the Buddha;
I am always thirsting for and yearning to see the Buddha, and for this reason, the fire of sorrow blazes intensely.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me the compassionate, cool, and refreshing water of the Dharma.
"By extinguishing this fire,
may the World-Honored One, out of compassion and immeasurable pity, grant me your presence, so that I may always behold the Buddha."
The World-Honored One constantly protects all humans and devas; for this reason, I now look up with thirsty longing, desiring to see him.
The body of a śrāvaka is like empty space, like a flame, a phantom, an echo, a transformation, or like the moon reflected in water.
The nature of sentient beings is like what is seen in a dream.
The sphere of the Tathāgata’s activity is as pure as lapis lazuli;
having entered the unsurpassed realm of the nectar-like Dharma, he is able to bestow immeasurable happiness upon sentient beings.
The sphere of the Tathāgata’s activity is subtle, wondrous, and profoundly deep;
no sentient beings are able to know it.
Neither the seers with the five supernatural powers, nor the śrāvakas, nor any of the pratyekabuddhas can know it either.
"I now have no doubt regarding the sphere of the Buddha's activity; I only pray that, out of compassion, you will manifest your body for me.
At that time, the World-Honored One arose from samādhi and, with a subtle and wondrous voice, spoke in praise:
“Excellent, excellent!
On this day, you have spoken these words most skillfully.
If all sentient beings hear this Dharma, they shall all enter the deathless gate of the non-arising of phenomena.”

Chapter 19: Entrustment (4) The Golden Light Sūtra, Chapter Nineteen: Entrustment At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha arose from samādhi and manifested great supernormal power. He stroked the crowns of the heads of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with his right hand, and addressed the various heavenly kings, dragon kings, and the twenty-eight divisions of the Great Generals of the Kṣitigarbha spirits, saying:

"For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges-sand kalpas, I have cultivated this subtle and wondrous *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama* Sūtra. You all should receive, uphold, read, and recite it, and widely proclaim this Dharma, ensuring that it is not severed within Jambudvīpa."

If there are good men or good women who, in future ages, receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, you gods should always protect them. You should know that such persons will constantly experience happiness among immeasurable hundreds of thousands of humans and devas in future ages, will encounter various Buddhas in future ages, and will swiftly realize and attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, the great bodhisattvas, along with the devas, nāga kings, and the twenty-eight divisions of the Great General Vaiśravaṇa, immediately rose from their seats, went before the Buddha, prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground, and together cried out:
"As the World-Honored One has commanded, we shall respectfully carry it out."
Thus they addressed the Buddha three times:
"As the World-Honored One has commanded, we shall fully carry it out.
Thereupon, the Great General Vajrapāṇi and the others addressed the Buddha, saying:

"As the World-Honored One has commanded, if in future ages there are those who receive and uphold this sutra—whether copying it themselves or having others copy it—I, together with these twenty-eight classes of spirits and ghosts, shall constantly attend upon and protect them, concealing their bodies. We shall cause all evils to be extinguished for these preachers of the Dharma so that they may attain peace and security; may you have no further concern."
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha manifested great supernormal powers, causing all the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions to tremble in six ways;
at that moment, all the Buddhas were filled with great joy, and because they entrusted this sutra to him, they praised those who uphold the Dharma and manifested immeasurable supernormal powers.

Thereupon, the great assembly of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, including the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa, Suvarṇaprabha, Suvarṇagarbha, Sadāprarudita, Dharmodgata, and others; as well as the Four Great Heavenly Kings, ten thousand devaputras, the Bodhi-tree goddess of the site of enlightenment, the Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā, and all the devas, humans, and asuras of the world—having heard what the Buddha had spoken, all resolved to attain the path of unsurpassed bodhi. Leaping for joy and filled with gladness, they paid homage and departed.

The Sutra of Golden Light, Volume Four: The Account of the Repentance for Eradicating Sin through the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*. Formerly, there was Zhang Judo, a District Magistrate of Wenzhou, a native of Jingcheng County in Cangzhou.
Before he had even taken office, he happened upon a slaughterhouse where cattle, sheep, pigs, chickens, geese, and ducks were being killed.
Less than ten days later, he suddenly fell gravely ill; his voice failed him and he became mute, dying shortly thereafter. Only his heart remained warm, so his family did not bury him immediately.
After three nights, he revived; he sat up and sought food.
When his relatives, both kin and non-kin, and neighbors from near and far heard of this, they all rushed there, young and old alike. As Jùdào was on the road, they spoke of the circumstances:

"At first we saw four men coming—one holding a staff, one holding a rope, one holding a sack, and one dressed in green. He rode a horse wearing a hat, dismounted at the gate, and called Jùdào to come forward. From his breast pocket, he drew out a document and showed it to Jùdào to look at; it was a joint lawsuit against Jùdào by pigs, sheep, and other animals. The text of the petition read:"

"Although pigs and other such beings have accumulated sins in previous lives and thus deserve to receive the bodies of animals, they are assigned to the world for a specific duration; once that period is complete and their retribution exhausted, they naturally become human again."

However, when pigs and other such beings calculate that their time for transformation from the bodies of animals has not yet arrived, they are nonetheless unjustly slaughtered while on the road; thus, with their allotted time remaining incomplete, they return once more to the realm of animals, where this single sinful body undergoes the blade and the blockage again. This is a matter of profound law that cannot be endured—please grant us your judgment.
Later, a judicial decision was reached, and the Office of Life-Span (Siming) was dispatched to pursue the transgression.

When the officers saw Ju Dao watching from the side of the road, they immediately called out for three men to come forward. One man tied a rope around Ju Dao’s throat, another took a bag to extract his vital breath, and a third struck him on the head with a staff and bound his two hands. They led him away, walking straight toward the north along a path.
When they had traveled halfway along the road, the messenger spoke to Juedao:

"When I was dispatched here, I examined your life tally and found that you ought not have died; however, it is because you killed so many sentient beings that you have been seized and sued by your enemies."
Judo immediately replied:

"In this secular world, people with their physical eyes do nothing but commit sins and fail to recognize good from evil. They see only that others in the world kill countless living beings, yet they do not see this evidence of retribution. Since I am the primary culprit for this misfortune and must die with my mouth sealed shut, by what means could I seek a path to life?"
"I blame myself for my past errors; regret can no longer reach them.

The messenger said, "The litigants before the Lord of the Dead number more than thirty heads, all hanging their spirits at the gate of King Yama, waiting for his arrival. As we enter the Way, we must pass by their side; not only is the royal law stern, but upon merely seeing these enemies, how could we avoid the suffering of being brought to our knees?"
Jiudao heard this and his terror increased all the more; at every step he fell to the ground. Those in front pulled him up by the rope, while those behind struck him with clubs.

Jiudao said, "I reckon my transgressions, and it is truly difficult for me to escape. If you would grant me one final plan, I might at least avoid meeting the face of my enemy; yet what can be done against the stern laws of King Yama?"
He sent a messenger to tell Juyao:

"If you can simply give rise to the aspiration for the sake of the sentient beings who were killed, and vow to have the four fascicles of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* transcribed, you shall obtain liberation."
Jujing, receiving the instruction, repeated the vow with a continuous voice:
"I vow to produce four fascicles of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* and offer them for the rest of my life, and I vow that my enemies shall be reconciled."

After a short while, he caught sight of the city gate. He sent someone to lead him eastward into a bend that turned north, where he saw before the hall of King Yama tens of millions of people undergoing interrogation and confession. They were bound with hoods, shackled, manacled, and fettered, while being subjected to flogging and beatings in such a chaotic and pitiful state that their cries of agony were unbearable to hear.
The messenger immediately reported the circumstances, and King Yama called out the man's name as he was brought forth for an audience.
The King said, "This man has committed extremely great transgressions; why were you negligent in apprehending him, allowing these pigs and others to file a complaint once more?"
He hurriedly summoned the accuser and brought him forward.
The messenger ran out in all directions, crying out and searching for the person whose life was being claimed, but could not find him; he returned to report to the king:
"I have searched everywhere for the pig and others, but they are nowhere to be seen."
The king immediately dispatched more people to search in various directions and inquire throughout the government offices, but everyone reported that he was nowhere to be found.
The king then commissioned the Great Deity of the Five Paths to inspect the records of transformed forms.
After a short while, an official came running with a document, which stated:

"According to an investigation, on that day, the person who received a good report from the Office of the World, Zhang Judo, because of his killing of living beings, vowed to produce four fascicles of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*. Based on the calculation of what he had encountered through killing, it is appropriate that he should, by virtue of this merit, transform his form according to his karma."

Regarding the directive "to issue a formal document and proceed with adjudication according to the Dharma": as for the complaint filed by the accuser of Zhang Judo, on that very day, the official document was issued in accordance with the office’s regulations, and it was ruled that [the deceased] had been transformed into a human being born within the world. This concludes the matter.
When the King saw this state of affairs, he was filled with extreme joy and said:

"Although Ju Dao has killed sentient beings, he was able to employ skillful means to make vows on their behalf and swiftly create merit, thereby causing these creditors to be reborn in the human realm. Since there is no opposing testimony and the matter cannot be taken at face value, I judge that Ju Dao shall be released to return once more to the path of life. You should maintain wholesome thoughts and cultivate much merit; sever your attachment to flavors and cease killing; do not again be stingy or greedy for wealth, nor fail to build bridges while instead devoting yourself solely to evil deeds."
Thereupon, he left the city as if returning from a dream.
While traveling along the road, he recounted this account; he inspired more than one hundred people to compose sutras, and those who abstained from meat and ceased killing were beyond counting.

This sutra is rare in the world; though I sought it everywhere without success, I traveled to various regions until I finally discovered it at Chanji Temple in Weizhou. I transcribed it and have kept it with me as an object of veneration.
Later, while residing in Dao and upon reaching the day he held office, his entire family, both young and old, completely abstained from meat.

His wife, who served as the Assistant Magistrate of Angu County in Wenzhou, fell ill; for a year she lost her voice and ceased eating, speaking only in delirium, chanting cries of pain and prostrating herself, pleading for the death penalty as if making a formal petition.
Juwu heard of this and explained it to her husband, saying:

"A condition such as this is most likely because the legal documents for the creditor’s claim on your life have not yet been finalized; therefore, your life has not yet ended. You should reflect deeply upon the causes and conditions that led you to take the lives of others, and urgently commission the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* and perform clear repentance and recitation."
"This scripture has no original copy nearby; it exists only within the household of the Daoist master.
While the County Vice-Magistrate was following its teachings and had hired people to transcribe the text, before the work was finished, his wife suddenly regained her senses and said:

'It was like a dream, in a state of profound confusion. Constantly there were pigs, chickens, geese, and ducks, passing by three times a day, vying with one another to bite and peck at me; the pain was unbearable. When they arrived as usual, they suddenly vanished from sight. There remained only a deluded pig, a deluded sheep, or some kind of chicken—all of which were human beings—coming to bid me farewell, saying:'"

"Although you were my enemy and subjected me to slaughter, because you created merit out of respect for me, it has enabled me to transform into human form; now that I have parted from my enemy, I shall not pursue further retribution."
Having finished speaking, he departed immediately.
From that time on, [the patient] no longer acted in such a manner; his illness was promptly cured, and he recovered to his original state.

At that time, throughout the entire prefecture of Wenzhou, those who raised chickens, pigs, geese, and ducks for meat all released their animals; every household ceased eating meat, everyone cultivated wholesome thoughts, and no slaughterhouses were established.
Furthermore, throughout neighboring prefectures and counties, reports have reached us that such pure practices have arisen concurrently in more than just one household.

As for the fact that there is currently no manifest efficacy in those who are being killed, this is because the karma of these sentient beings has reached its full measure and they are destined to die; therefore, there is no retribution [to be seen].
It is merely that they exhaust their human lifespan and are reborn as animals, where they are slaughtered by others.

If sentient beings meet with slaughter before their allotted life span is exhausted, they will immediately be subject to legal accusations from the world and suffer sudden death; or they may endure debility and illness for years and months, crying out in pain or speaking deliriously even in their sleep—all of which results from the karmic attachments of sentient beings, for only when the records of their fate are finalized does their life truly end.

All various transgressions are extinguished through repentance, yet only the sin of killing is not removed by repentance alone; this is because one has an enemy who pursues one with a focused intent for retribution. Unless one personally and suddenly creates scriptures or images for that person’s sake, or unless one is dispatched by others or finds the circumstances too difficult to restrain, the act of killing will not cease. In such cases, one should give rise to shame and remorse, and offer lamentations for the harm caused.

When one kills with a blade as if slicing off a piece of pork, or sells it to others to obtain wealth for one's own abundance, one must perform the ritual of confession and recitation clearly and individually for each instance, so that this merit may be dedicated to the enemy, enabling them to be reborn quickly in the human realm.
Lawsuits shall cease of their own accord, and no further arrests or summons shall be issued.
Good men and women alike should take heed of this tomorrow.
